name: Frontend
quote: People keep talking about the frontend and backend. What's the difference?
summaryLead: The layer people directly see, click, and type into
summaryRest: On a sign-up page, the fields, submit button, and pending, success, or error messages belong to the frontend; whether the account was actually created must come from the backend result.

name: Component
quote: Turn this repeated product area into a component so one change updates every instance.
summaryLead: A component is a unit that groups a reusable piece of interface with the behavior it owns.
summaryRest: For example, a product card can be shared by the home page, search results, and saved items when all show an image, price, and purchase action. An input field can also be a component. Components divide interface responsibility; not every tiny label needs to become one.

name: Markdown
quote: The document AI wrote is full of # signs and asterisks. What is that, and can it turn into nicely formatted text?
summaryLead: Write structured text with lightweight punctuation
summaryRest: Markdown uses simple characters for headings, lists, links, code, and emphasis. It is convenient for documentation and content stored as plain text. Different renderers support different extensions, so preview the actual output and treat embedded HTML carefully.

→
RENDERED · After rendering

sections.html:
Markdown≠Rich-text editor

Markdown uses punctuation for headings, bold text, and lists, so you edit plain text. A rich-text editor shows formatted content directly, like a familiar document app.

When to use it

  • Organize context for AI with headings, lists and code blocks
    # Requirements
    - The home page needs a sticky navigation bar
    - Use blue buttons    Use headings and lists to express requirements so AI can recognize the hierarchy.
  • Save structured AI output for further editing
    Weekend plan
    · SaturdayHiking
    · Rest on Sunday    Many chat products render Markdown-style text as headings and lists.
  • Write README files and project documents as versionable plain text
    README.md
    # My first page
    ## How to run
    - npm install    Plain text works in many editors, making it easy to save and review over time.
  • Keep plain-text notes readable across editors
    README.md
    # My first page
    ## How to run
    - npm install    Plain text works in many editors, making it easy to save and review over time.

When NOT to use it

  • Paste without checking Markdown support: preview first, or convert to plain text
    # Weekly update **completed**: home-page redesign - bug fixesThe target chat box does not parse Markdown, so # and ** appear literally.
  • Convert or export separately when Word is required, keeping the original .md file
    Wnotes.md → Save as notes.docx
    Conversion may change Markdown structure or escape some characters.
  • Use repeated spaces or arbitrary line breaks for alignment across renderers
    Price　　　¥199
    In stock　　　42    Markdown collapses consecutive spaces; use a table or list for layout.
  • Open a fenced code block without closing it, so later prose becomes code
    ```
    npm run dev
    The body text below also became code    A missing closing backtick makes the following content parse as a code block.

name: CSS
quote: The button works, but its color stays gray. Help me find which style is overriding the theme color.
summaryLead: CSS is a style language that describes a web page's appearance, layout, and changes across available space.
summaryRest: For example, HTML may already contain a button while the button is still gray or overflows on a phone. The browser matches CSS rules and calculates a final style from their priority and order. CSS controls presentation; it does not implement the business logic that runs after a click.

name: DOM
quote: A task appears after I click Add, but it is not in the source HTML. Help me confirm what was inserted at runtime.
summaryLead: The DOM is the node tree the browser uses to represent and modify a web document.
summaryRest: For example, the source HTML may contain one task while a click adds another to the page. A script created a node and inserted it into the runtime DOM. That change affects the current page, but whether it survives a refresh depends on separate persistence in a backend or browser storage.

summaryLead: The HTML title that identifies the current document
summaryRest: The browser uses it in a tab or window title, and a search system may use it when generating a result title. It should distinguish the current page, but the page H1 and a search result title are not the same field.

name: Undo
quote: This change is wrong—undo it and put things back the way they were before I touched them.
summaryLead: Undo rolls your last action back exactly as it was—Ctrl+Z brings the wrongly deleted row back, no retyping.
summaryRest: Press Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on Mac) to step backward, and redo to step forward again if you go too far. It has limits: usually only the last several steps, and the history is gone after refresh or close—important deletions still deserve a confirmation rather than relying on undo.

name: Accessibility
quote: I heard some people browse without a mouse, using a screen reader—check whether they can use this page properly.
summaryLead: Accessibility means more people can use your page in more situations—not only with a mouse, not only with perfect vision, and even read aloud by a screen reader.
summaryRest: You test with a mouse and good eyes, but visitors may use a keyboard, a screen reader, or squint at a phone in sunlight. Accessibility extends "works for me" to those situations: text alternatives on images, buttons reachable by Tab, sufficient text contrast. When an AI reply mentions a11y, it is the shorthand for this word (a plus 11 letters plus y).

sections.html:
Input≠Search input

A search input is an Input with a specific purpose and may include submit, clear, or suggestion behavior. A normal input can collect any short value, such as a name or email.

Input≠Autocomplete

Input accepts text. Autocomplete offers possible matches as someone types.

When to use it

  • Account and contact details
    oil-oil••••••••
    Sign in
  • Search queries
    🔍 Search topics you are interested in…
  • Short names and titles
    NameAlex Chen
    Emailyou@example.com
  • Single-line codes or values
    title2026 Product Plan v3

When NOT to use it

  • Collect a long answer that needs several lines
    This component’s interaction design is very thoughtful…
  • Use placeholder text as the only label
    StatusIn progress
  • Wait until final submission to reveal every obvious error
    Name"Name" disappears after you type.
  • Show read-only content in a field that looks editable
    Versionv2.4.0
    It looks editable, but it is not.

name: Segmented
quote: Put two or three choices side by side so people can tap one to switch, like the iPhone control.
summaryLead: Switch quickly between a few short, exclusive modes
summaryRest: A segmented control keeps several short options visible together. It often changes a view, sort order, or time range and usually does not navigate to a new page. If options are numerous or their labels are long, choose another control.

sections.html:
Segmented≠Button

Segmented contains mutually exclusive choices: selecting one clears another. A Button or button group runs actions and does not imply exclusive options.

When to use it

  • List or grid view
    ListKanbanCalendar
  • Short time ranges
    PreviewSource
    The content stays the same; only the view changes
  • Sort mode
    DayWeekMonth
    A small set of short labels is easy to scan
  • A few mutually exclusive display modes
    TodayThis weekThis month

When NOT to use it

  • Use it for many long choices
    OverviewSettingsLogs
  • Treat it as primary page navigation
    AllFrontendBackendDesignOperationsTestingToo many options squeeze each label and make scanning harder
  • Use icons whose meaning is not obvious
    PriorityLowMediumHigh
    Submit
    If it only takes effect on submit, radio buttons are clearer
  • Use it as an on-off setting; choose a Switch
    OnOff
    For two states, a switch is easier to use

sections.html:
Collapse≠Accordion

A collapse panel is any content that can expand and close. An accordion is usually a group of collapse panels and often allows only one open panel at a time.

When to use it

  • Frequently asked questions
    How do I reset my password?▾
    Which payment methods are supported?▸
  • Advanced settings
    Notifications
    Advanced settings▸
  • Long supporting details
    Basic information▸
    Member permissions▾
  • Optional sections in a compact page
    ▸ More settingsCollapse secondary details to shorten the page

When NOT to use it

  • Hide critical information or a required action
    ⚠ Your account may be at risk. Take action now.▸
    A critical notice is collapsed by default, so people miss it on arrival
  • Nest several levels of collapsible panels
    About this project▾
    One content group doesn’t need an extra expand step
  • Make the heading too vague to predict the content
    AllAwaiting paymentCompleted
  • Collapse everything when most people need it open
    Level 1 group▾

    Level 3 group…▸

summaryRest: A progress indicator helps people understand the state of an upload, installation, or multi-step task. Use a percentage when the total is known; otherwise show ongoing activity without pretending to know the finish time. State success, failure, and cancellation clearly.

sections.html:
Progress≠Spinner

Progress uses a track to show overall completion and can show a percentage when it is measurable. Spinner usually marks a brief local wait with no known completion ratio.

Progress≠Steps

Progress shows continuous completion. Steps names the stages so people know where they are in a process.

When to use it

  • File upload
    📎 design-file.sketch66%
  • Import or export
    Getting started3/5
  • Installation
    Storage6.6 / 10 GB
  • A task with measurable completion
    Exporting 1,024 records…42%

When NOT to use it

  • Show a fake percentage when progress is unknown
    Loading, please wait…
  • Leave a completed task stuck below 100%
    Saved
  • Use animation without a readable status
    66%Storage used
  • Hide failure or cancellation behind the same loading state
    Uploading…12%
    Stuck at 12% for 10 minutes.

name: Steps
quote: Checkout has three steps. Show people which step they're on at the top.
summaryLead: Show progress through a task with several required stages
summaryRest: A step indicator shows where the user is in a fixed process such as checkout or setup. Use clear stage names, mark completed and current steps, and explain whether people may move backward. It should reflect real task progress, not decorate ordinary sections.
demoHtml: ✓Fill in the information 2Confirm order 3Complete payment

sections.html:
Steps≠Progress

Steps shows named stages in order. Progress is better for continuous work such as upload or processing completion.

Steps≠Spinner

Steps helps someone complete a multistep task. Spinner only says the system is processing; it does not move the person to a new step.

Steps≠Number Input

In systems such as Material Design, Steps can also be called a Stepper for a multistep flow. The plus/minus control beside an Number Input may use the same name, so say steps indicator or number stepper when clarity matters.

When to use it

  • Checkout
    1Enter information2Confirm order3Complete payment
  • Account setup
    1Basic information2Contact information3Finish
    Name
    Next
  • Application process
    1Place order2Pay3Receive order
    Step 2, one step left
  • A fixed sequence with a clear finish
    1Create account2Complete your profile3Get started

When NOT to use it

  • Use it for optional tabs or categories
    1Comments2History3Save
    These are peer sections; use tabs
  • Hide how many stages remain
    1Avatar2Nickname3Signature
    Either can be filled in first, so these aren’t steps
  • Allow jumping ahead when required data is missing
    1Fill in2Verify3Agreement4Survey5Upload6Review7Finish
    Too many steps increase the burden; combine unnecessary ones
  • Change the order after the process begins
    1Enter email2Enter password3Finish
    A simple login doesn’t need multiple steps

sections.html:
Header≠Navbar

Header is the complete top page area and can include brand, search, and sign-in. Navbar is the portion dedicated to primary navigation.

When to use it

  • Use a page header when the brand, primary navigation, and account controls need to stay together at the top.

    New version released · Check for updates

When NOT to use it

  • Cram every navigation link and action into the header, making important actions hard to find.
    Brand · Product · Solutions · Customers · Pricing · Docs · Blog · Events · Careers · Search · Sign in · Sign up
  • Make a fixed header so tall that it obscures content while the user scrolls.
    The fixed header takes up nearly half the screen.
  • Omit both a brand marker and a link home, leaving users unsure which site they are on.
    ProductPricingHelpSign in
  • Treat the page header and Navbar as the same thing. Distinguish them by the top-level container and their navigation role.
    ProductPricingDocs

name: Masonry
quote: The images are all different heights—do not crop them into one size, just let new ones tuck under the short ones.
summaryLead: Pack cards of different heights into equal-width columns
summaryRest: On galleries and inspiration feeds, images vary in height; masonry lets each new card fill the shortest gap so no full row is left blank. sections.html:
Masonry≠Card Grid

Card Grid keeps strict rows and equal-height cards for scanning and comparison; Masonry drops row alignment for compactness and suits browsing.

Masonry≠Bento Grid

Bento Grid assigns cell sizes to express a designed priority; Masonry positions come from an automatic packing rule and express no priority.

When to use it

  • Gallery walls where photos and illustrations keep their natural ratios
  • Inspiration and asset feeds built for continuous browsing
    Keep scrolling to load more
  • Product or case covers with inconsistent sizes that should stay compact
    Noise-canceling headphones¥ 899

  • Growing collections where packing saves more height than tidy rows

When NOT to use it

  • Content with a strict order, such as steps or timelines
    Step 1Step 2
    Step 4 lands ahead of Step 3
  • Row-by-row comparison of similar fields, where misalignment hurts
  • Keeping multiple columns on phones until cards become too narrow
  • Long-form article lists, where packing breaks continuous reading

Split-screen≠Sidebar

In Sidebar the sidebar is navigation with clearly less weight than the workspace; in Split-screen both sides carry near-equal, independent tasks.

Split-screen≠Image plus text

In an image-plus-text row the image only serves the text; in Split-screen each side carries its own task or entry, and removing either one loses a real job.

When to use it

  • Login and signup pages: brand story on one side, the form on the other
    Brand introLogin form
  • Two audience entries: personal vs business, buyer vs seller
    PersonalBusiness
  • Two product paths: start a trial vs book a demo
    Start a trialBook a demo
  • Two plans or versions compared side by side at similar weight
    Plan A · annual billingPlan B · monthly billing

When NOT to use it

  • One side is only a decorative image while the other holds the only task
    All content sits on the right
  • A wide content area with a narrow sidebar is a sidebar layout instead
  • Keeping the side-by-side split on phones until text and buttons shrink
  • Cramming both halves full until the first screen becomes two crowded pages

sections.html:
Typography≠Heading

Typography is the full system of text roles and styles, including headings, body copy, and supporting text. A heading is only one text role that marks page or section hierarchy.

When to use it

  • Create clear levels for page, section, and item headings
    Page titleSection title
  • Keep long body text comfortable to read
    Body text needs a readable size and line height for long-form reading.
  • Make dates, notes, and other supporting details quieter
    Website redesign v2In progress
    Alex Chen updated 3 days ago · visible only to you
  • Emphasize a small number of truly important words
    This update fixed 12 issues; the payment flow changed the most, so test it carefully.

When NOT to use it

  • Use so many heading styles that the hierarchy disappears
    Heading 1Heading 2Heading 3Heading 4Heading 5
  • Set body text too small or too light to read comfortably
    This is an important instruction, but it uses 10px light-gray text that’s hard to read.
  • Bold a whole paragraph when only one point needs emphasis
    When every word is bold, nothing reads as the real priority.
  • Use spaces and line breaks to force alignment; use Space
    Name: Alex Chen
    Phone: 138 0000 0000    Full-width spaces break alignment when the font changes

name: Dark Mode
quote: Add real dark mode: text, borders, charts, and code blocks must switch with the page.
summaryLead: Dark mode is a switchable dark interface theme state, not merely a page with a black background.
summaryRest: When someone chooses dark mode or their system prefers it, backgrounds, text, borders, buttons, charts, and focus states need coordinated, sufficiently contrasting values. It serves different environments and preferences. A single dark poster or visual style is not automatically a switchable theme.

name: Design Token
quote: Organize the main color, spacing, and radius as design tokens instead of repeating values in every component.
summaryLead: A design token is a named variable that centrally stores and reuses design values such as color, spacing, and typography.
summaryRest: A primary button color can be named color.brand.primary and a common gap space.16; components reference those names rather than each hard-coding a color or pixel value. Tokens help a shared rule stay consistent across a site, component library, or other interfaces when themes or brands change. They are not a synonym for every CSS variable and do not replace the design decision itself.

name: Contrast
quote: That gray helper text on the page strains my eyes—make it readable.
summaryLead: Contrast is the brightness difference between text and background—big enough to read; light gray on light gray is not.
summaryRest: Light gray body text on a gray background almost vanishes when you squint—that is insufficient contrast. To turn "hard to read" into a checkable requirement, tell the AI "keep body text at 4.5:1 contrast against the background," the common industry threshold. Dark mode fails here most often: black backgrounds paired with the old gray look layered but sit below the line.

name: Visual Hierarchy
quote: This page feels chaotic—everything is the same size. Layer it: headline dominant, description secondary, button most visible.
summaryLead: Visual hierarchy makes visitors read the page in your intended order—headline first, description next, button last.
summaryRest: Where the eye lands first on a page is not random: size, color, and position steer it. The headline is biggest and boldest so it lands first; the description sits one shade lighter so it reads second; the button carries a fill so it pops last. A page that "looks messy" usually has everything equally large and equally heavy, leaving the eye nowhere to start.

HTTP vs HTTPS: what is the difference?

Use HTTPS for public sites and production APIs. It keeps HTTP's request-response rules while TLS protects the connection.

Decision pointHTTPHTTPS
What it isThe standard request-and-response rules between client and server.Standard HTTP traffic carried over an encrypted TLS connection.
Data in transitPlain text; network observers along the path can read or modify data.Encrypted in transit; protected from eavesdropping and silent tampering.

name: Cookie

A cookie is only part of the request round trip, not a complete authentication system, authorization decision, or database; sensitive sessions also need properties such as Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite.

summaryRest: When a page on app.example.com requests api.example.com, the server must allow that page origin in its response before the browser gives the data to script. It protects cross-origin reads in browsers; the server still decides whether an API can be called and whether a user has permission.

name: Validation
quote: People can submit complete nonsense. How do I stop bad input before it gets saved?
summaryLead: Check that incoming data has the expected shape and allowed values
summaryRest: A required field can be checked when someone leaves it, while cross-field rules usually need a submit-time check. Frontend feedback helps people correct mistakes, but the backend must validate again and return specific field errors.

name: Enqueue
quote: After upload, do not keep the page waiting. Enqueue the transcoding task, return a task ID, and let me check its status later.
summaryLead: Enqueue puts work into a queue so a request can receive a task ID before a later processor runs it
summaryRest: After someone uploads a video, the API can enqueue a transcoding task and return a task ID while the page shows queued, processing, or completed. Batch notifications can use the same pattern. A successful enqueue means the queue accepted the task, not that transcoding or delivery has finished; queues also do not automatically promise FIFO ordering or exactly-once processing.

name: Idempotency
quote: A payment callback may arrive more than once, but the same order must count as paid only once.
summaryLead: A repeated request produces the same intended business effect instead of applying it again
summaryRest: If a payment provider retries the same callback concurrently after a timeout, the order service uses its stable event id as a unique key and atomically claims processing so the order is marked paid only once. Idempotency does not mean zero logs, notifications, or other side effects, and different business operations must not share one key.

name: Message Consumer
quote: The message was sent, but the queue keeps growing. Check whether a consumer is receiving, processing, and acknowledging the messages.
summaryLead: A message consumer is an application or instance that receives messages from a queue, handles them according to its rules, and acknowledges their processing status
summaryRest: An upload API can publish a transcoding task while a consumer takes it from the queue and runs the work. An order system can use a consumer to receive an order-created message and create a shipping record. Without a consumer, messages build up; if processing fails, a message may be delivered again, so successful publishing is not business completion.

ConsumersRabbitMQ ↗

name: Browser Storage
quote: Keep this draft after refresh, but do not treat it as a database shared by every user.
summaryLead: Browser storage is a local web mechanism for keeping data in a person's current browser.
summaryRest: It can remember dark mode, an unsubmitted form draft, or recently viewed projects so a later page load may restore them. It normally belongs only to that browser and device; clearing data, changing browser, or switching device may remove it.

name: Database
quote: The content people submit disappears after a refresh. We need somewhere to actually save it.
summaryLead: Store and find application data such as users, posts, and orders
summaryRest: After someone publishes a post, the backend stores it so it remains available after refresh or sign-in. CRUD names the four common operations: create, read, update, and delete. Data kept only in one browser does not automatically appear on another device.

name: Database Migration
quote: I need to add a phone column to our user table, but production already has tens of thousands of rows. How do we update the schema without losing data or causing downtime?
summaryLead: An ordered, versioned, and traceable set of steps for changing database structure or required data.
summaryRest: Suppose users already contains live rows and a required status column is needed. A safe migration adds a compatible column, backfills old rows, verifies that no NULL values remain, and only then enforces the constraint. The migration tool records applied versions, but migration files are not data backups and do not guarantee lossless reversal.

summaryLead: Ask a relational database to read or change structured records
summaryRest: SQL can select, filter, join, insert, update, and delete data in relational databases. Parameterize user values instead of building query strings, and inspect indexes and execution plans when a query becomes slow. A correct query still needs authorization around it.

Quick decision

SQL vs NoSQL: which fits your data?

SQL is a query language; the actual choice is between a relational database and a specific NoSQL database. Compare them by data relationships, access patterns, and consistency needs—not by assuming one is faster.

Decision pointRelational (SQL)NoSQL database
Data structureStores structured records in tables and connects related data through fields.Uses models such as document, key-value, wide-column, or graph.
Decision pointOften the direct fit when joins, constraints, and transactions matter.Can fit a well-defined data model and access pattern with a purpose-built product.
Typical fitOrders, accounts, and other related business records that need consistency.Key-value caches, documents, event records, or graph relationships.
Creating an e-commerce order

When an order connects customer, inventory, and payment records, a relational database is often the direct fit. If logs are mainly written and read by device ID at high volume, a purpose-built key-value or document database may fit better. NoSQL products differ widely, so test the specific product against the real workload.

name: Transaction
quote: Creating an order and deducting stock must succeed together; if any step fails, it must not leave half an order behind.
summaryLead: A group of related database operations that are committed or rolled back as a whole
summaryRest: When an order is created, the system usually writes the order record and deducts inventory together. If stock is unavailable, the order should not remain. A transaction rolls back this group of operations in the same database, but it does not automatically undo external actions like payments or emails.

name: Database Write
quote: The API says saved, but the nickname returns to its old value after refresh. Confirm the write really committed.
summaryLead: Writing new or updated data to a database and committing the change
summaryRest: After a user changes a nickname, the backend must complete and confirm the database write so refresh can read it back. A successful response alone does not prove that, and a write is not the same as backup, replication, or immediate visibility everywhere.

name: PostgreSQL
quote: AI suggested using Supabase and PostgreSQL for my users and orders; how is that different from saving files?
summaryLead: An open-source database management system that stores and queries related data in tables
summaryRest: For example, store users and orders in separate tables and require each order to reference an existing user. PostgreSQL can enforce that constraint, but the rule must be configured; installation alone does not define your business rules.

name: Backend
quote: Where does the part users can't see run, and who handles things like login and saving data?
summaryLead: The server-side part people usually cannot see that handles requests and data
summaryRest: After someone submits a sign-up form, the backend checks the phone number and code, creates the account, and returns success or failure to the page. Passwords, secret keys, and permission rules belong here, not only in the interface.

quote: Is there a ready-made framework for building the backend, so I don't have to start from scratch?
summaryLead: Use a shared structure for routes, requests, data, and server behavior
summaryRest: A backend framework supplies conventions and tools for routing, input handling, middleware, databases, and responses. It reduces repeated setup, but it does not decide the product's rules for you. Choose one that fits the language, hosting model, and size of the application.

name: Atomicity
quote: When two users buy the last item at once, there cannot be two successful orders; checking and deducting stock must act as one whole operation.
summaryLead: The property that related operations either all take effect or none of them does
summaryRest: When two people buy the last item at the same time, checking and deducting inventory must be an indivisible whole so one succeeds and the other fails. Atomicity covers only the defined operation scope; it does not make every distributed step across systems roll back together.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
atomic packageGo ↗TransactionsPostgreSQL ↗

name: Process
quote: The image worker crashes and takes down the whole site. Put that work in a separate process and verify the web service stays available.
summaryLead: A process is a running program together with the separate resource environment assigned by the operating system.
summaryRest: A web server and image worker can run as separate processes with different process IDs and isolated memory. If the image worker crashes, it can restart independently while the web process keeps serving. A process is neither a program file nor a whole machine; one machine can run many processes.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
multiprocessing — Process-based parallelismPython Documentation ↗

name: Thread
quote: Two requests update the same cache. Confirm whether they are threads in one process and make the shared-state order explicit.
summaryLead: A thread is an execution path inside a process, and threads in one process usually share memory and resources.
summaryRest: A service process can use several threads for concurrent requests. Threads A and B can both access the same cache; sharing helps communication but can cause overwrites and races. A thread is not an independent process with fully isolated memory, and actual parallelism depends on the runtime and workload.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
threading — Thread-based parallelismPython Documentation ↗

name: Coroutine
quote: Do not block the execution path while an endpoint waits on external services. Suspend the coroutine and let other work proceed.
summaryLead: A coroutine is a lightweight execution unit that can suspend at explicit points and resume later.
summaryRest: When an endpoint calls three external services, coroutines can yield at each await so the same thread advances other work, then resume when responses arrive and combine results. A coroutine is not a new thread and does not guarantee parallelism; CPU-heavy work is not automatically faster.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Coroutines basicsKotlin Documentation ↗

name: Message Queue
quote: Don't make the user stare at a spinner while generating this huge report. Put the job into a message queue and let background workers process it.
summaryLead: A communication and decoupling mechanism that temporarily stores messages between senders and receivers so neither must wait synchronously.
summaryRest: When a user exports a large report, the API creates a job, writes its ID and parameters to a queue, and immediately returns a pending status. A worker generates the file and updates the same ID to completed or failed. Enqueueing proves receipt, not completion, and retries can cause the same job to be delivered again.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
What is a Message Queue?AWS ↗RabbitMQ Core ConceptsRabbitMQ ↗

name: Side Effect
quote: A user is only previewing a price. Do not silently write an order or send email; do that only after explicit submission.
summaryLead: A function or request changes external state or triggers an external action beyond returning a value
summaryRest: A price preview can calculate and return shipping without creating a quote or sending email. Saving the order and notifying the user are intentional side effects when the user explicitly submits. A side effect is not automatically an error; it needs a clear trigger and observable result.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Functional Programming HOWTOPython ↗TransactionsPostgreSQL ↗

name: Lock
quote: Two requests decrement the last item concurrently. Lock the shared record so one proceeds and the other waits and rechecks.
summaryLead: A lock is a concurrency-control mechanism that limits simultaneous access to a shared resource.
summaryRest: When two requests update one inventory record, the lock owner checks and decrements before release; the waiter then rechecks, so only one succeeds. The lock must cover the correct resource. Inconsistent acquisition order can deadlock, and an in-process lock does not automatically protect another service instance.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Explicit LockingPostgreSQL ↗

name: Race Condition
quote: Coupons occasionally oversell while one test run looks normal. Reproduce the race with concurrent timing, fix it, and verify repeatedly.
summaryLead: A race condition occurs when the ordering of concurrent operations changes the final result.
summaryRest: Two requests can read and issue the last coupon at nearly the same time, so the read-write order decides whether overselling occurs. Race conditions are broader than data races; request ordering, file state, or event timing can also race, and one passing test does not prove absence.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Data Race DetectorGo Documentation ↗

name: Backpressure
quote: When downstream processing cannot keep up, do not let the queue and memory grow forever. Slow or pause the upstream and resume after recovery.
summaryLead: Backpressure sends a downstream slowdown or pause signal upstream to limit new or unfinished work
summaryRest: If an image-processing service can finish only a small number of tasks per second while uploads keep arriving, queue length and memory grow without backpressure. The system can slow or pause publishing, or cap unacknowledged work, then resume when capacity recovers. Backpressure is not extra capacity and is not a fixed rate limit independent of downstream state.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Flow ControlRabbitMQ ↗

name: Lease
quote: Two scheduler instances must not run the same summary. Let one hold time-limited ownership, let it expire after failure, and let the other take over.
summaryLead: A lease is time-limited ownership that must be renewed and can be taken over after it expires
summaryRest: If two scheduler instances can run the daily summary, one can acquire and renew a lease while the other waits. If the holder fails, the lease expires and a waiting instance can take over. A lease only decides who may take over: a delayed old holder can still write, so each takeover also needs a larger fencing token that the write target checks atomically to reject stale holders.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
LeasesKubernetes Documentation ↗Use fencing tokens to reject expired holdersRedis Documentation ↗

name: Distributed System
quote: Orders, inventory, and payment run in different services. When a service or network fails, show exactly how far the order got.
summaryLead: A distributed system uses multiple computing nodes that coordinate over a network to achieve a system goal.
summaryRest: During checkout, order, inventory, and payment services may run separately and exchange requests and results over a network. An inventory timeout does not mean every service stopped, so the system must handle partial failure. Multiple threads in one process share process resources and are not automatically a distributed system; the important boundary is network communication and independent failure.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
How to build reliable systems with unreliable componentsGoogle Cloud ↗

name: Authentication
quote: How do I verify that someone is who they say they are? I need to add sign-in.
summaryLead: Verify who is making the request
summaryRest: Authentication proves an identity through a password, passkey, one-time code, or trusted provider and then maintains a session. Store credentials safely, limit repeated attempts, and protect recovery paths. After identity is known, Authorization still decides what that person may do.

name: Audit Log
quote: An administrator changed a permission. Show who changed what, when, and whether the action succeeded or was denied.
summaryLead: An audit log records who did what to which object, when, and with what result.
summaryRest: After an administrator changes the billing-editor role, an audit log can record the actor, time, target, action, and success or denial so the permission change can be investigated. It is different from an error log that explains a program failure and from monitoring that observes health signals; request data may contain sensitive information, so its scope and access need control.

name: Entitlement
quote: A user bought a Pro subscription; how should the backend check if they can access this export feature?
summaryLead: The specific features and allowances granted to an account by its plan or authorization
summaryRest: In this drawing-tool example, Free allows three generations while Pro includes HD export. Payment and access activation are separate: the server needs effective entitlements and checks every restricted action. Changing a Free label in the browser does not grant access.

name: Cache
quote: The new styles are deployed, but some people still see the old version. Find out which cache layer has not updated.
summaryLead: Keep reusable results so later requests do not always return to the origin
summaryRest: When new CSS is deployed but an old style remains visible, the browser, a shared cache, or a CDN may still be reusing an older copy. Caching reduces waiting and repeated transfer; diagnose the layer that served the old result, because clearing one browser does not prove a shared cache or origin has changed.

name: SEO
quote: Help me clarify this product article's title, body hierarchy, and links so both readers and search engines can understand it.
summaryLead: SEO is ongoing work that helps search engines understand, discover, and present web content.
summaryRest: A help article that truly answers a question with clear headings, body structure, and reachable links is easier for search systems to understand; product pages also need accessible content and links. SEO improves the conditions for understanding and presentation, not a guarantee of a particular keyword rank.

name: Canonical URL
quote: Keep the product's campaign URLs accessible, but declare the parameter-free URL as canonical and use it in the sitemap.
summaryLead: A preferred representative URL for pages with the same or very similar content
summaryRest: Several product URLs with campaign parameters can remain accessible while each page declares a parameter-free representative URL in its head and the sitemap lists that same address. A canonical is usually a hint to search systems, not a browser redirect; use a redirect when visitors must move.

name: XML Sitemap
quote: The new article is live but has few internal links. Generate a sitemap.xml containing only valid canonical URLs.
summaryLead: List important canonical URLs in a machine-readable XML file for crawler discovery
summaryRest: When a new article has few internal links, listing its full address in sitemap.xml can help crawlers discover and request it. It is a machine-readable URL list, not visitor-facing site navigation, and it does not guarantee indexing or ranking.

name: Robots.txt
quote: Limit crawler access to duplicate filter paths, but do not use robots.txt as permission for the admin area.
summaryLead: A root-level file that tells automated crawlers which paths they may crawl
summaryRest: Shopping carts and duplicate filter URLs can waste crawler requests, so robots.txt can describe crawling rules at the site root. It is guidance for crawlers that follow the rules, not a block on normal visitors, authentication, or protection for sensitive data.

name: Not Found Page
quote: This article URL no longer exists. Make a real 404 page that still lets people return to the article list.
summaryLead: Return 404 for a missing resource and give people a way to recover
summaryRest: When an article link no longer works, the server should return 404, explain that the content was not found, and offer a list or search path. A Not Found message alone is not enough: Network must also show HTTP 404. If the content moved to a new address, use a redirect instead.

name: Env Var
quote: I know a secret key shouldn't go in the code. Where should I put it?
summaryLead: Provide configuration outside the source code
summaryRest: Environment variables supply values such as API endpoints, feature settings, and secret keys when a program starts. Public browser variables are visible to visitors, even if their names come from an environment file. Keep real secrets on the server and document the required variable names with safe examples.

name: Deployment
quote: I finished the site. How do I make it available at a URL that other people can open?
summaryLead: Build the project and make it available on a server
summaryRest: Deployment turns source code into a running website or service. It may install dependencies, build assets, set environment variables, start processes, and connect a domain. A repeatable deployment includes logs, health checks, and a way to return to a known working version.

The platform hosts static files, functions, or services based on its configuration and provides the runtime environment
Public websites usually have addresses assigned by the platform; internal services may only be accessible on private networks or between services

Further reading
Publishing your websiteMDN ↗

name: Web Hosting
quote: Confirm that this project has hosting that can continuously serve the site, then deploy it publicly. Do not treat localhost as live.
summaryLead: A service that continuously stores and serves website files or a running environment
summaryRest: A page that works locally still needs a public environment that can serve it continuously. Web hosting provides that environment for files or a running service; deployment is the one-time action of publishing a version into it. They are related but not the same.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
What is a web server?MDN ↗Web server glossaryMDN ↗HTTP Semantics: ServersRFC Editor ↗

name: CD
quote: Send this CI-passing version to testing first; production needs human approval unless we explicitly choose continuous deployment.
summaryLead: CD keeps verified versions continuously releasable, or releases them to production automatically under defined rules.
summaryRest: Continuous delivery keeps a version through the pipeline and ready to release, with a possible human approval before production. Continuous deployment automatically releases to production after gates pass. Both are more than “tests run automatically”; the key difference is whether production keeps a human approval.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Continuous deploymentGitHub Actions ↗

name: Staging
quote: Deploy the candidate to staging with production-like configuration and de-identified order data; do not run destructive verification in production.
summaryLead: Staging is an isolated pre-production environment used to validate a candidate release under production-like conditions.
summaryRest: A candidate version can run in staging with separate services, test payment, and de-identified orders so the team can check a full deployed flow. Staging is one kind of test environment, not a name for every local, CI-ephemeral, or test URL; its defining role is production-like validation before production.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Using deployment environmentsGitHub Actions ↗

name: Monitoring
quote: After release, monitor login error rate and checkout success rate; alert above a threshold and show which version was running then.
summaryLead: Monitoring continuously observes production metrics, logs, and alerts to find anomalies and judge system health.
summaryRest: A login error rate can cross a threshold, trigger an alert, and connect its time window, request logs, and running version. This provides signals from real use after release. One test report only records some checks at one time and cannot replace production monitoring.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Google SRE: Monitoring Distributed SystemsGoogle SRE ↗

name: Rollback
quote: When a new version sends login error rate sharply up, roll back to the last known-good version; then confirm both running version and metrics recover.
summaryLead: Rollback restores a system or configuration to a previous known-good state to stop current impact.
summaryRest: If v2 causes abnormal login errors, switch the running image or configuration back to v1 and check the live version, login result, and error rate recover. It aims to reduce impact first. Fixing the issue and shipping a new version later is a forward fix, not rollback.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Kubernetes Deployment rollbackKubernetes ↗

name: Feature Flag
quote: Open the new recommendation feature to employees first; if error rate rises, turn off the new path immediately without redeploying.
summaryLead: A feature flag enables or disables a code path at runtime according to configuration or user conditions.
summaryRest: The same deployed code can send employees to a new recommendation page while other people stay on the old path; closing the flag stops the new path on anomaly. It separates deploying code from deciding who gets a feature. Permanently deleting code or restoring a whole old version is not a feature flag itself.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Feature flagging introductionOpenFeature ↗

name: Canary Release
quote: Send 5% of users to the new release first; expand only while error rate stays healthy, and return to the stable release on anomaly.
summaryLead: A canary release exposes a new version to a small amount of real traffic before health signals decide whether to expand or stop.
summaryRest: Checkout v2 can serve 5% of requests while stable v1 keeps the other 95%; if v2 crosses its error threshold, its traffic returns to v1. This limits exposure to a release version. It is not merely switching one feature on or off inside the same release.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Canary deploymentsAWS ↗

name: Blue-Green Deployment
quote: Keep blue serving while deploying and accepting the new release on green; switch production traffic only after it passes.
summaryLead: Blue-green deployment runs old and new releases in two production-capable environments, then switches traffic after the candidate environment is verified.
summaryRest: Blue can keep travel site v1 live while green independently runs v2; after login and booking checks pass, the production entry switches to green and blue remains temporarily available for return. Two application environments do not automatically isolate or make the database compatible.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Blue/Green deployment methodologyAWS ↗Blue-green deployment in Azure Container AppsMicrosoft ↗

name: Serverless
quote: I only have a small feature. Is there a way to run code on demand without buying or managing a server?
summaryLead: Run backend code on demand without managing a long-running server
summaryRest: A serverless function is deployed to a managed platform and starts when an HTTP request, schedule, or event triggers it. It reduces server operations for small independent tasks, but runtime limits, cold starts, regions, and stateless execution still shape the design.

sections.html:
Anatomy
API gateway→Function instance→External status
The platform handles URLs, HTTPS, scaling, and request routing.
Your code runs when a request or event arrives.
Persistent state lives in databases or storage, not function memory.

name: Server Logs
quote: There's an error in production. Where can I see what happened on the server?
summaryLead: Record what the server did so problems can be traced
summaryRest: Server logs capture requests, errors, background jobs, and important state changes. Useful logs include time, severity, and a request or job identifier. Avoid recording passwords, tokens, and unnecessary personal data, and connect related events so one failure can be followed across services.

name: Circuit Breaker
quote: The payment dependency keeps timing out. Stop making every request wait, fail fast or degrade, and probe it again after a pause.
summaryLead: A circuit breaker cuts off a repeatedly failing dependency, fails fast or degrades, and probes recovery later
summaryRest: When a checkout page calls a payment dependency that keeps timing out, continuing to wait and retry can exhaust the caller's threads and request queue. A breaker moves through Closed, Open, and Half-Open: normal calls pass while Closed; repeated failures open it for fast failure or fallback; a later limited probe tests recovery, returning to Closed on success or Open on failure. It is different from one timeout or retry and cannot repair the dependency.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Circuit Breaker PatternMicrosoft Azure Architecture Center ↗

name: Single-Instance Deployment
quote: Run this service as one instance and explain the short outage during restart, while separating in-memory task risk from durable data.
summaryLead: Single-instance deployment keeps exactly one running replica of a service in its environment.
summaryRest: A background service with a replica count of 1 sends requests to one running instance. A release or crash restart can make it briefly unavailable, and in-memory work that was not written to durable storage may be lost. Single-instance deployment is not the Singleton pattern and does not mean data cannot be durable: it describes the number of runtime replicas, while a database or other durable store can exist separately.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
ReplicaSetKubernetes ↗

name: Multi-Instance Deployment
quote: Run several instances to share requests, but keep users logged in when their next request reaches another instance.
summaryLead: Multi-instance deployment runs multiple instances of the same service that receive requests together.
summaryRest: A load balancer can send requests to instance-a and instance-b, so another instance can serve traffic when one restarts. If a login session lives only in one instance's local memory, a user may be logged out after the next request reaches another instance; the state must be shared or externalized. Multiple instances can improve service redundancy and throughput, but they do not automatically make a database highly available or solve concurrency coordination and consistency.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
ReplicaSetKubernetes ↗Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets overviewMicrosoft Learn ↗

name: User Story
quote: Before listing features, explain who has the problem, what they need, and why it matters.
summaryLead: A brief requirement that states who needs what and why from the user's perspective
summaryRest: A traveler may need to save an unfinished itinerary so they can continue on another device. A user story starts a requirements conversation but does not replace interaction details, acceptance criteria, or technical design.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
What are User Stories?Agile Alliance ↗User Story TemplateAgile Alliance ↗

name: Use Case
quote: Write the refund request end to end: how the customer starts, how the system responds, and what failure looks like.
summaryLead: A description of the main interaction and important exceptions between an actor and a system while reaching a goal
summaryRest: For an order refund, a use case states eligibility, what the customer submits, how the system responds, and how expired or duplicate requests end. It describes observable behavior without prescribing internal code.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
What Is a Use Case?Figma ↗Defining Use CasesIBM ↗

name: User Flow
quote: Map out every step a user takes from arriving on the site to finishing checkout.
summaryLead: A path diagram of the steps and branches a user takes to reach one goal
summaryRest: A sign-up flow might show entering the sign-up page, filling in details, verification success or failure, and account creation. It keeps the steps that affect progress, not every click on the screen.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
What Is a User Flow?Figma ↗

name: User Journey
quote: Map the whole experience from first hearing about the product to actually using it, including where people get stuck.
summaryLead: A staged view of a user's actions, thoughts, feelings, and obstacles across touchpoints while pursuing a goal
summaryRest: A learner might discover a course through a friend, visit its page, pay, receive an email, and enter the first lesson. A user journey needs interview or behavioral evidence and must not present team assumptions as real feelings.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
What Is a User Journey Map?Figma ↗What Is a Customer Journey Map?Figma ↗

name: PRD
quote: Help me spell out what I'm building for the AI: the problem it solves and what counts as done.
summaryLead: A product document that defines the user problem, scope, and success criteria
summaryRest: Before a team builds one-click meeting-notes export, a PRD explains who needs it, what this release includes, and how the team will know it worked. It aligns product, design, and engineering without locking every technical detail.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
How to create a product requirements document (PRD)Atlassian ↗

name: Product Discovery
quote: Don't have AI start coding features yet. Let's do product discovery first to see whether users actually care about this problem.
summaryLead: The exploration process of collecting user and business evidence to validate whether a problem is real, valuable, and feasible before committing to full development.
summaryRest: Suppose a team wants to build a prompt-result comparison tool. Discovery turns 'creators need comparisons' into a testable assumption, then gathers evidence from recent real stories and a low-fidelity task. The evidence may support continuing, narrowing, changing direction, or stopping. Discovery reduces early uncertainty; it does not guarantee product success.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
What is Product Discovery?Atlassian ↗Continuous Discovery HabitsProduct Talk ↗

name: MVP
quote: Let's start with the smallest version that proves the core feature works instead of building everything at once.
summaryLead: The smallest real product or experiment that tests a key product assumption
summaryRest: To test whether freelancers will pay for payment reminders, a team can charge real customers and deliver the reminders manually first. An MVP gathers decision-worthy evidence; it is not a carelessly stripped-down full product.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
What Is an MVP?Lean Startup Co. ↗What is a Minimum Viable Product (MVP)?Atlassian ↗

name: Product Backlog
quote: Put these requests and problems into an ordered backlog, but do not treat every item as a delivery promise.
summaryLead: A dynamic, ordered list of features, fixes, and improvements that a product may need next
summaryRest: When a trip app receives both a payment incident and a map-export idea, the team can reorder items using product goals, risk, and new evidence. Items near the top are usually clearer, but backlog inclusion does not promise a date or delivery.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
The Scrum GuideScrum Guides ↗

name: Product Roadmap
quote: Turn the next few stages into a roadmap that explains why and what to improve, without scheduling daily development tasks.
summaryLead: A dynamic plan that communicates product goals, priorities, and expected outcomes across time horizons
summaryRest: A trip product might use Now for reliable saving, Next for collaborative editing, and Later for testing automatic planning. A roadmap communicates direction and tradeoffs; distant work rarely supports exact date commitments.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Agile RoadmapsAtlassian ↗

name: Gantt Chart
quote: Put design, development, testing, and launch on a timeline with dependencies, and show what a delay changes.
summaryLead: A schedule chart that uses timeline bars to show task dates, duration, milestones, and dependencies
summaryRest: A release can require interaction design before development and testing. If development moves, dependent testing and the launch milestone move too. A Gantt chart exposes schedule impact, but unknown durations should not become invented dates.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Work with the Gantt Chart ViewMicrosoft Support ↗What Is a Gantt Chart?Atlassian ↗

name: Wireframe
quote: Hold off on colors—sketch a gray page skeleton first: header, hero, three cards, footer, just the positions.
summaryLead: A wireframe is the page skeleton drawn in gray blocks and placeholder lines—it fixes "what goes where" before any colors or fonts.
summaryRest: Sketch the page in gray blocks first: how tall the header is, what sits in the hero, where the button goes. With positions settled, colors and fonts can be adjusted without reworking the layout. The wireframe fixes positions; the visual design handles colors and fonts.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
WireframeWikipedia ↗

name: Moodboard
quote: Here are my references: the three I like set the feel, the crossed-out one is what to avoid. Style the site this way.
summaryLead: A moodboard collects reference images, colors, and keywords on one board—align on "what feeling" before building the page.
summaryRest: "Make it premium" or "give it breathing room" rarely means the same thing to you and the AI. Collect five or six screenshots you like, one or two you dislike, and the main color, then send the collage—working from pictures lands far closer than adjectives. Fixing a wrong direction at the collage stage means swapping a reference; after the page is built, it means redoing the work.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Mood boardWikipedia ↗

name: Heuristic Evaluation
quote: Don't just say this interface 'feels clunky'. Run through Nielsen's usability heuristics to pinpoint whether status is hidden, error prevention is missing, or terminology is confusing.
summaryLead: A usability inspection method where evaluators systematically check an interface against established design principles to identify interaction defects.
summaryRest: An evaluator edits a nickname in Settings and clicks Save. With no saving state or result message, the issue is recorded under visibility of system status with its location, reproduction steps, impact, and recommendation. After the fix, the same task is repeated to verify visible progress and outcome. Heuristic evaluation can reveal likely issues early, but it does not replace testing with real target users.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
How to Conduct a Heuristic EvaluationNielsen Norman Group ↗10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface DesignJakob Nielsen ↗

name: A/B Test
quote: Do not choose between these sign-up pages by taste. Randomly split users and compare the same metric.
summaryLead: An experiment that randomly assigns eligible users to variants and compares them using predefined metrics
summaryRest: Eligible new visitors can be randomly shown one of two sign-up pages during the same period, then compared on completion rate. A before-and-after comparison or changing metrics mid-test does not provide the same causal evidence.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Experiment Types in Web ExperimentationOptimizely ↗Run A/B TestsOptimizely ↗

name: Conversion Funnel
quote: Turn visits, sign-up starts, profile submissions, and completions into a funnel to find the largest drop-off.
summaryLead: A sequence of user counts and conversion rates that locates drop-off from entry to a target outcome
summaryRest: Out of 1,000 visitors, 620 may start sign-up, 310 submit details, and 280 finish. A funnel shows how many remain at each step. Mismatched event definitions, time windows, or user scopes can make the shape misleading.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Funnel ExplorationGoogle Analytics Help ↗

name: CRUD
quote: Build me a client quote list: add new ones, edit amount and status, delete rows, and show all records on open.
summaryLead: CRUD is the four basic operations repeatedly performed on one kind of data: create, read, update, and delete.
summaryRest: For a client quote list: tapping "new" adds a quote (create), opening the list shows every record (read), changing an amount or status is an update, and removing a record is a delete. These four cover the backbone of managing data; exports and charts are extra features built on top, not one of the four.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Create, read, update and deleteWikipedia ↗

name: Field
quote: Each quote should record client name, amount, date, and status—just these four, nothing more for now.
summaryLead: A field is one standalone piece of information in a record, such as client name, amount, or date.
summaryRest: One client quote consists of four fields: client name, amount, status, and date. Before building a tool, splitting "what I want to record" into a field list matters more than sketching pages: the list drives the form, the list view, and validation. The field is the information itself; the input is just the control for filling it in.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
HTML formsMDN ↗

name: Data Type
quote: The amount column is stored as text and cannot be summed. Change it to a number type, and switch date to a real date picker.
summaryLead: A data type is the format agreement for one piece of information: text, number, date, or an on/off value.
summaryRest: If the amount field is a number type, phones show a numeric keyboard and records can be summed; stored as text, it can neither compare nor total. A date type opens a date picker and enables time sorting. The type fixes the format before entry, while validation checks at submit—two things that happen in order.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
<input> typesMDN ↗

name: Import & Export
quote: Add an export button to the quote list that downloads all records as a CSV that opens cleanly in Excel.
summaryLead: Import and export move data in bulk: export saves records into files like CSV or Excel, import turns a file back into records.
summaryRest: Export 200 quotes as a CSV for the accountant, and import the edited file back—data moves between tools as files. Both operate on whole batches, not single records. If Excel shows garbled Chinese, it is usually an encoding problem; ask the AI to re-export as UTF-8.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Comma-separated valuesWikipedia ↗

name: Acceptance Criteria
quote: Write clear acceptance criteria for the itinerary feature: saving shows the trip, refresh keeps it, and invalid dates explain how to fix them.
summaryLead: Acceptance criteria are checkable conditions that determine whether a result is acceptable.
summaryRest: For an itinerary, saving can show the trip, refresh can keep it, and an end date before the start date can explain how to correct it. This turns “mostly done” into observable results. Code coverage or framework choice alone cannot prove the user need is complete.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
ISTQB GlossaryISTQB ↗

name: Test Case
quote: Write a failed-login test case so another person can use the same account and steps and see the same result.
summaryLead: A test case is one repeatable check that states preparation, action, input, and expected result.
summaryRest: Prepare a registered account, enter its email with a wrong password, submit, and expect an explanation without entering the account page. This lets people or automation check the same thing. “Test login” is a test plan, not one executable case.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
ISTQB GlossaryISTQB ↗

name: Unit Test
quote: Add unit tests for price calculation: 100 gets 20 off, 99 does not, and external payment must not participate.
summaryLead: A unit test tests one independently verifiable function, component, or small module.
summaryRest: Pass a fixed price to a tax function and assert the amount, or check that a disabled button does not submit. It isolates outside services so a failure points to a small responsibility. A full login with browser, API, and real database is not a unit test.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
ISTQB GlossaryISTQB ↗

name: Integration Test
quote: Test that submitting a registration form sends correct fields, the API saves them, and the page shows server errors.
summaryLead: An integration test verifies that multiple modules or dependencies cooperate correctly.
summaryRest: A registration form sends a name to an API, the API writes a database, then returns success or error to the page. This finds mismatched field names, formats, and error handoff. A pure calculation function with fixed input remains a unit test.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
ISTQB GlossaryISTQB ↗

name: Contract Testing
quote: The backend renamed a field in the response, and our frontend crashed on deploy. How can we catch this automatically on commit?
summaryLead: An automated test that records the requests and responses a consumer truly depends on, then verifies that the provider remains compatible.
summaryRest: A profile page may read avatar_url and nickname. A consumer test records the request and minimum response; provider verification compares the backend's real response with that contract. Renaming avatar_url to avatar then fails CI before merge. This checks communication at a service boundary, not the whole page, network, or business calculation.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
What is Contract Testing?Pact Docs ↗Contract TestsMartin Fowler ↗

name: End-to-End Test
quote: Like a real user, create an itinerary from the travel home page, save it, reopen it, and confirm the confirmation page shows that same trip.
summaryLead: An end-to-end test follows a complete system flow from a user's entry point to the final result.
summaryRest: A browser can register, sign in, create a trip, and reach confirmation across pages, services, and data storage. This is evidence that the user journey works. Calling one API or checking one function is important but not end-to-end.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
ISTQB GlossaryISTQB ↗Playwright testing and fixturesPlaywright ↗

name: Smoke Test
quote: After a new version reaches testing, first check that home opens, login works, and the core API responds; if one fails, do not start full regression.
summaryLead: A smoke test uses a few critical checks after a new build to decide whether the system is worth deeper testing.
summaryRest: A new version can open home, log in, and call a core API first; any failure blocks slower tests. It aims to decide “continue or stop” within minutes. Re-running every old feature and edge case is regression testing, not smoke testing.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
ISTQB GlossaryISTQB ↗

name: Regression Test
quote: After changing tax rules, rerun payment, coupons, and order confirmation as well as the new rule to ensure working checkout was not broken.
summaryLead: Regression testing checks that a change has not broken functionality that previously worked.
summaryRest: After tax changes, rerun payment, coupons, and confirmation; after dependency upgrades, rerun critical pages. It selects old capabilities the change could affect, not only the new request. A new feature working does not prove no regression.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
ISTQB GlossaryISTQB ↗

name: Test Coverage
quote: Do not only report “90% coverage”; also show whether the high-risk path combining payment failure and a coupon was actually tested.
summaryLead: Test coverage measures how much of requirements, code structure, or risk paths have been reached by tests.
summaryRest: Branch coverage can show whether the coupon-plus-payment-failure combination was reached; a requirements matrix can show a missing payment case. Coverage finds untouched paths. It does not mean no defect or meaningful assertions, even at 100%.

name: Test Double
quote: When testing an order failure message, use a controllable payment test double that returns “payment rejected” instead of depending on the real payment service every time.
summaryLead: A test double is a controllable object that replaces a real dependency during testing.
summaryRest: When an order module requests payment, a double can reliably return success, rejection, or timeout so tests verify how the page handles each. Mock, stub, fake, and spy can be different kinds of test double; not every double is simply a Mock, and it cannot prove a real service is connected.

name: Test Data and Fixture
quote: Prepare fixed user and product data for the order test, and create it before every run and clean it after so the next run starts identically.
summaryLead: Test data are input and state samples; a fixture is a reusable setup and cleanup mechanism.
summaryRest: A fixed user and order JSON are test data. Creating an account and order before a test, then deleting or restoring state afterward, is a fixture. Together they give each case the same start. One random input or yesterday’s leftover record is not stable evidence.

sections.title: Further reading

ISTQB GlossaryISTQB ↗Playwright testing and fixturesPlaywright ↗

name: Flaky Test
quote: Run the same commit five times: it sometimes passes and sometimes times out. Check waiting conditions and shared accounts first; do not hide red with endless retries.
summaryLead: A flaky test sometimes passes and sometimes fails when the code has not changed.
summaryRest: The same CI commit can time out occasionally, or parallel tests can race for one account and alternate red and green. Unlike a defect that fails every time, flakiness makes the result untrustworthy. Retries can collect clues or temporarily reduce impact, but do not replace finding timing, shared-state, or environment causes.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
ISTQB GlossaryISTQB ↗Playwright testing and fixturesPlaywright ↗

name: Load Testing
quote: Before the event, simulate many real checkout users and show how latency, throughput, and error rate behave at the target load.
summaryLead: Load testing measures latency, throughput, and errors while a system handles a realistic level of load.
summaryRest: Before an event, an isolated production-like environment can simulate browsing and checkout with synthetic or sanitized data. The team records response time, throughput, and failures, then compares them with predefined thresholds to decide what to improve. Load testing is not the same as pushing a system to its breaking point with stress testing, and it cannot promise zero production failures.

name: Quality Gate
quote: Why is my Pull Request blocked with an error saying 'Quality gate failed'?
summaryLead: A set of conditions that decide whether code may be merged or a release may proceed
summaryRest: All tests may pass while coverage remains below the agreed 80%, keeping a pull request blocked. Checks produce results and the gate evaluates them; branch protection must require that result to enforce the merge restriction.

name: Terminal
quote: AI gave me a command to run, but I don't know what it will do. Is it safe to run?
summaryLead: Run text commands in a specific folder on your computer or server
summaryRest: A terminal gives you a prompt where commands can start tools, install packages, inspect files, and run a project. The current directory changes what a command affects. Read the command and confirm the path before running anything that changes or deletes files.

quote: AI told me to install dependencies, and one command downloaded a ton of stuff. What's going on?

name: Build
quote: Build this commit into a deployable front-end artifact and retain a version identifier; do not treat “build succeeded” as being live.
summaryLead: A build converts source code, dependencies, and configuration into a runnable or releasable artifact.
summaryRest: Front-end source can build into a dist folder and service code into a versioned container image. A successful build means that commit produced the requested artifact. Making it available in testing or production is a later deployment and release step.

Further reading

name: CI
quote: For every PR or merge, automatically run lint, build, and key tests, with results shown on the pull request.
summaryLead: CI is the practice of automatically building and testing changes as they enter shared code, so integration problems appear early.
summaryRest: A PR can automatically run lint, unit tests, and build, then write pass or fail back to the PR. This exposes issues before or just after merging. Manually testing once before release is not continuous integration.

sections.html:
Further reading

name: Lint
quote: Use lint to flag unused variables and unhandled promises first, but do not say a passing lint means the button really works.
summaryLead: Lint is static checking that uses source rules to find suspicious patterns and consistency problems without running the full program.
summaryRest: Lint can locate unused variables, clear mistakes, or unhandled promises and make the warning disappear after a correction. It finds source-level risks early. Clicking a button and confirming save results or API responses still need build, tests, or manual verification.

Further reading

name: Hash
quote: I updated the website, so why does it still show the old content?
summaryLead: A digest computed from content using a specified algorithm, often used to compare files or identify versions
summaryRest: A website build can include a script’s content hash in its filename to distinguish old and new files. The page must also reference the new file to load the update. Different contents can collide, so a hash is not an absolutely unique identifier.

name: Tech Stack
quote: When someone asks what tech stack I use, what am I supposed to say?
summaryLead: The set of languages, frameworks, data services, and tools used to build and run software
summaryRest: A website might combine JavaScript, React, a database, build tools, and hosting. They handle different jobs: page behavior, interface, data, and operation. Start by learning what the project already uses before replacing several layers at once.

name: JavaScript
quote: What language makes the interactive parts of a webpage move and respond?
summaryLead: A programming language that makes a web page respond to actions and data
summaryRest: When someone marks a task complete, browser JavaScript can send a request, receive the updated list, and change that row on the page. JavaScript can also run on a server through Node.js, which is a different environment with different responsibilities.

name: TypeScript
quote: I've heard there's a stricter version of JavaScript that catches mistakes early. What is it?
summaryLead: A language that checks written code for mismatched names and value types before it runs
summaryRest: If you type user.nmae instead of user.name, TypeScript can flag it before the page runs when the object type is known. It checks declared code contracts; passing those checks does not prove the product logic is right.

quote: What's the language everyone recommends for automating spreadsheets and files with a script?
summaryLead: A programming language often used to automate work on a computer or server
summaryRest: A Python script can read three Markdown notes and write their titles into summary.csv. It runs on a local machine or server; an ordinary web page does not execute a local Python script by itself.

quote: I only wanted to edit this draft, so why did the original settings change too?

summaryRest: When two names point to the same settings object, editing its contents changes what both names read. JavaScript object references help illustrate this relationship, but do not expose directly manipulable memory addresses.

quote: People keep saying to use React for websites. What's better about it than writing the page directly?
summaryLead: A JavaScript library for building interactive interfaces from components and state
summaryRest: After an item is added to a cart, React can update the count from 2 to 3. Whether the item was actually saved and remains after a refresh still depends on backend and data storage.

quote: Is Vue really friendlier for beginners, and how is it different from React?
summaryLead: A JavaScript framework for building interactive interfaces with templates and components

quote: Is there a framework for building a full React site with routing and SEO?

name: Tailwind CSS
quote: Do I really have to open a separate CSS file for every style change? Can I adjust styles right where I write the markup?
summaryLead: A utility-first CSS framework that styles elements through small class names
summaryRest: Classes such as p-6, rounded-xl, and border give a card padding, rounded corners, and a border. Tailwind generates CSS rules; the same CSS layout rules still explain why something overlaps or crowds.

name: AI Application Basics
quote: Add an AI assistant to my website that people can chat with.
summaryLead: A product that uses an AI model, an interface, and sometimes tools to help people complete tasks
summaryRest: When you ask a calendar assistant about tomorrow afternoon, the interface receives the question, the model decides what to look up, a calendar tool reads the real schedule, and the app shows the result. The model does not enter the calendar on its own.
