name: AI Hallucination
quote: This AI travel guide sounds confident, but I do not want to trust the opening hours. Research the official website or reservation page online and include the source link and update date.
summaryLead: An AI hallucination is information a model generates that looks credible but is inaccurate, unsupported, or invented.
summaryRest: An AI can invent venue hours, a nonexistent link, an outdated rule, or a function that is not in a project. Fluent wording is not evidence. An Agent can research changing external facts online, but conclusions still need official or original sources, tool results, tests, and human judgment.

name: Vibe Coding
quote: I can't code. I just want to tell an AI what I need and have it build it for me.
summaryLead: Building software by describing the desired result to an AI agent and reviewing the work it makes
summaryRest: You can ask an agent to build a settings page, inspect the changed files, then test the mobile layout. It can speed up implementation, but you still need to define the scope, check the result, and protect data and secrets.

name: Multimodal AI
quote: Can AI understand my screenshot too, not just the text I send it?
summaryLead: AI that can combine information such as text, images, audio, or video in one task
summaryRest: Send a screenshot of a phone checkout page with the question “Why is the payment button missing?” and the AI can consider both the visible layout and your written question.

name: Context Engineering
quote: As the task gets longer, the AI starts missing a newly confirmed requirement. What should the next turn include?
summaryLead: Organizing the goals, rules, source material, and latest results an AI receives for each turn
summaryRest: For a long login fix, keep the current error, relevant files, and the rule that shared components cannot change. Repeated logs can become a summary with a path to the original.

name: Token
quote: Everyone says AI pricing is based on tokens. What is a token, and how does it relate to what I type?
summaryLead: A small piece of text or code that a model reads and writes
summaryRest: Models split text, punctuation, and code into tokens using their own rules. Input and output token counts affect available context, wait time, and cost; a token is not always one word or one character.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Counting tokensOpenAI ↗

name: Context Window
quote: The AI forgets what I said at the start of a long chat. Does it have a memory limit?
summaryLead: The total amount of input and output a model can process in one request
summaryRest: After a long chat, “follow the first requirement” can fail if that requirement was not included in the current request. More context capacity does not make every piece of information relevant.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Conversation stateOpenAI ↗

name: System Prompt
quote: Where do I set rules for the AI, like its tone and what it can or can't answer?
summaryLead: Instructions an AI product gives the model behind the scenes to guide its behavior
summaryRest: A support assistant can be told to hand off refunds above $500. That rule can shape its reply, but real permission checks must still control whether a refund happens.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Text generationOpenAI ↗

name: Conversation History
quote: The earlier messages are still visible in the chat. Why did the AI edit the wrong second item?
summaryLead: Conversation history is the earlier messages a product saves and can include again when they matter to a new request
summaryRest: When you say “make the second one shorter,” the application retrieves the three earlier titles and includes the relevant material in this request. A complete transcript in the interface does not mean the model received every message this time.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Conversation stateOpenAI ↗

name: Prompt
quote: Build a client quote list: client name, amount, date, and status, stored in the browser, newest first.
summaryLead: A prompt is the message you send the AI—the problem, requirements, and context all live in it, and it steers what the AI builds.
summaryRest: "Build a client quote list with client, amount, date, and status, stored locally, newest first"—that whole sentence is the prompt. The AI reads it before every move: specific wording lands specific results, while "make a nice tool" forces guessing. When results disappoint, refine the prompt before switching tools—add the object, the requirements, and what counts as done.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Prompt engineering guideAnthropic ↗

name: Stateless Request
quote: The table is still visible in the chat. Why does the AI not know what to do when I send only “continue”?
summaryLead: A stateless request is a model call that uses only what it receives this time and does not automatically retain prior input or results
summaryRest: If one request creates a table and the next contains only “continue,” the model does not know which table to continue. The product may save the table and chat, but it must include the current goal, table, and relevant result again.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Conversation stateOpenAI ↗

name: Structured Output
quote: AI gives me a big block of text I can't use directly. Can it return the answer in a fixed format?
summaryLead: Model output returned in an agreed, machine-checkable shape
summaryRest: To fill a calendar form from an email, a product can require fields such as title, date, and location with defined types. JSON is a common encoding, not the same thing as structured output, and business rules still need validation.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Structured model outputsOpenAI ↗

name: Streaming Response
quote: Show the answer as it comes in, like someone typing, instead of making me wait for the whole thing.
summaryLead: A response sent and displayed in consecutive pieces as it is generated
summaryRest: A chat answer can appear as if it is typing. An early first piece makes waiting feel shorter, but the full answer can still take time to generate and transmit.

sections.title: Further reading
sections.html:
Further reading
Streaming API responsesOpenAI ↗

name: AI Agent
quote: I don't want to direct every step. Can I give it a goal and let it figure out how to finish it?
summaryLead: An AI system that can plan steps, use permitted tools, and act on results toward a goal
summaryRest: To fix a page, an agent can read the relevant file, edit it, run a check, and report what passed. It only has the tools, permissions, and context the product gives it.

sections.html:
Quick decision

AI agent vs chatbot: what is the difference?

A chatbot describes the conversational interface; an AI agent describes a goal-directed workflow that uses results to decide the next step. One product can be both.

Decision pointAI AgentChatbot
What it describesA workflow that takes actions, observes results, and continues toward a goal.An interface where people and an AI exchange messages.
How work continuesUses tool output or other observations to choose another action or stop.Organizes interaction as turns; it may answer directly or provide access to an agent workflow.
Typical workflowInspects repository files, edits code, runs tests, and verifies fixes before concluding.Explains why an error occurred based on text pasted into the chat prompt.
Investigating an application bug

A chatbot can explain an error from the details you provide. An AI agent can take on the goal of fixing it: read files, edit code, run tests, and use the results to decide whether more work is needed. A chat interface may be how you control that agent.

Further reading

name: Harness Engineering
quote: The same AI works well sometimes but repeats the same mistake elsewhere. What can I change besides the model?
summaryLead: The engineering practice of turning project knowledge, tools, state, permissions, and checks into a working environment an AI agent can use
summaryRest: For example, when a frontend agent delivers a plausible page, an independent evaluator can operate the live flow and return failed steps and screenshots to the next turn. Harness engineering changes the conditions around the model rather than making the prompt longer.

quote: The AI can research the itinerary and flights, but it must ask me before paying or issuing a ticket.
summaryLead: Pausing an AI workflow before a critical decision or high-risk action so a person can review, approve, reject, or correct it
summaryRest: A travel agent may search and compare flights automatically, but before payment it should show the dates, passenger, total, and change rules and wait for approval. Human-in-the-loop adds decision points where they matter rather than making a person watch every step.

name: Sub-agent
quote: Can I split a big task among a few helpers at the same time, then get one combined result?
summaryLead: A separate agent the main agent assigns to a bounded part of a larger task
summaryRest: Before release, a main agent can ask one sub-agent to review copy and another to check mobile layout, then combine their evidence. Each sub-agent needs a clear scope, permissions, and expected return.

name: Tool Calling
quote: AI can talk, but how do I get it to actually check the database or make a request?
summaryLead: A model’s request for an application to run a named tool with parameters
summaryRest: A model can request a calendar lookup, but the application must validate the permissions and parameters before it reads the schedule. The returned result, not the request text, proves what happened.

name: ReAct
quote: Can the AI check the result after each step before deciding what to do next?
summaryLead: A task pattern where an agent decides, acts with a tool, observes the result, and decides again
summaryRest: When a login button does nothing, an agent can inspect the button first. If the click handler already exists, that observation changes the next action to inspecting the network request and its 401 response.

name: Agent Loop
quote: After a check fails, should the AI continue editing, stop to ask me, or end the task?
summaryLead: A runtime mechanism that repeatedly calls AI and tools, then uses check results to continue, pause, or stop
summaryRest: While fixing horizontal overflow in mobile navigation, the first failed check can start another round. A second identical failure or a change to shared styles pauses for confirmation. The task ends only after the build and 390px page check both pass.

name: Provider
quote: What do Provider and Model mean in this configuration, and where will my request actually go?
summaryLead: A platform or infrastructure entity that hosts, runs, and serves large language models through APIs.
summaryRest: A model vendor, cloud platform, aggregation gateway, or even a local model service may appear as a Provider in a tool. It receives requests and provides model access, often handling credentials, rate limits, or billing, but it does not necessarily train or directly run the underlying model. Check the Base URL, key issuer, and billing party to identify the actual path.

name: Base URL
quote: I've switched the model API endpoint to our team's self-hosted proxy. Where do I update the Base URL to make it work?
summaryLead: An address prefix shared by a group of API requests, onto which specific endpoint paths are appended.
summaryRest: For example, one client may combine https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with /chat/completions to form the full request URL. Whether /v1 belongs in the prefix and which path the client appends depend on both the service and the client. Check both sets of official documentation instead of applying one fixed pattern.

name: API Proxy
quote: Requests started working after I switched to a relay URL. Check who can see the prompts, files, and key along that path.
summaryLead: An intermediate service that receives and forwards requests and responses between a client and an upstream API.
summaryRest: For example, an AI tool can send a request to a relay, which forwards it to a model provider and returns the result along the same path. The relay may handle authentication, routing, or a shared gateway, but that does not mean the model runs there. Prompts, file fragments, and credentials may pass through it, so verify the operator, privacy policy, retention rules, and key issuer before use.

quote: My AI tool only has settings for OpenAI, but I want to use DeepSeek. Can I just swap the Base URL and API Key?
summaryLead: A third-party model endpoint conforming to OpenAI request and response formats, allowing compatible clients to switch providers seamlessly.
summaryRest: For example, a tool that only sends OpenAI-shaped requests may connect to another model service after changing the Base URL, API key, and model name. The service may implement that shape directly or through a translation layer. Compatibility usually covers only some endpoints and fields, so tool calls, images, streaming, and other capabilities still need separate checks.

name: API Key
quote: Connect the LLM API for me; read the API Key from environment variables, and never hardcode its value in the source code.
summaryLead: An authentication credential used by applications to prove identity, verify permissions, and track resource usage with an API service.
summaryRest: For example, a web app can read an API key from an environment variable and send it with an AI request. The service usually associates permissions and usage with the key's account, project, or application—not necessarily a specific person. A leaked key may spend quota or expose data, so keep it out of source code, repositories, and chat logs, then revoke and replace it immediately if exposed.

name: Configuration File
quote: Help me update the default model in the AI tool's config file to DeepSeek, and increase the timeout limit to 60 seconds.
summaryLead: A structured file containing runtime settings and environment parameters for software to parse upon startup or runtime.
summaryRest: For example, an AI tool may read its model, endpoint, timeout, and permission settings from a config file, while project rules describe the stack and collaboration conventions for the current codebase. A config may reference secret variable names, but real secrets belong in environment variables or a secret manager and must not be tracked by git.

name: Profile
quote: Configure two profiles for me: 'work' using our company's private API, and 'personal' using my own API Key. Show me how to switch between them.
summaryLead: A named and saved collection of configuration settings for switching between work, personal, or different provider environments.
summaryRest: For example, work and personal projects may use separate Providers, Base URLs, key variable names, or permission settings saved as work and personal profiles. Selecting a profile loads its configuration; it does not switch git branches, project files, or conversation history, and it does not replace checking the actual endpoint and credential source.

name: Project Rules
quote: I keep reminding the AI to use TypeScript and our existing styles. Can these requirements live in project rules?
summaryLead: Repository-level instruction files that inject team stack requirements, coding conventions, and operational boundaries into an AI agent.
summaryRest: For example, a team can record its stack, code style, validation steps, and operating boundaries in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another file supported by the tool. Whether it is loaded, which directories it covers, and its precedence are product-specific. Rules reduce repetition but do not guarantee compliance or replace permissions and tests.

name: Hook
quote: Does this tool support a post-write Hook? If so, have it format only the files that just changed.
summaryLead: An automated mechanism that intercepts execution upon specific lifecycle events to run predefined scripts or checks.
summaryRest: For example, Git can run a check before committing, and some AI tools provide an event after writing a file. The specific event names, parameters, and whether a failure blocks later steps depend on the product. Review the current tool documentation before configuration, and keep dangerous scripts bounded by permissions.

name: Plugin
quote: AI plugins, hooks, and Skills all look like extensions. Which one actually fits this need?
summaryLead: A distributable software package installed into a host application to provide extended capabilities, commands, or UI via standardized extension points.
summaryRest: For example, an editor plugin can add a sidebar, shortcuts, code completion, or diff previews. Other plugins may only add commands or service integrations. A plugin does not require a UI, and it is not the same as a Skill task method or a Hook event script.

summaryLead: A connection protocol AI applications use to discover and call external tools, data, and prompts
summaryRest: When a user asks who owns issue #1024, the application discovers get_ticket from an MCP server and sends the lookup. The issue tracker checks read permission and returns Alex. MCP standardizes the connection; it does not replace the real system or its authorization.

quote: I have to teach the AI the same process every time. Can it remember how to do this task?
summaryLead: A specialized workflow and instruction package organized in a standard directory, with SKILL.md as the entry point for agents to execute on demand.
summaryRest: A Skill can include instructions, scripts, references, and templates. When a task matches it, an agent reads those materials and follows the documented method.

name: Permission Mode
quote: Routine changes inside this project can continue automatically, but ask before deletion, wider access, or external actions. Which permission setting fits?
summaryLead: A set of control presets defining file system boundaries, network access limits, and user confirmation triggers for an AI agent.
summaryRest: For example, one Codex permission option can allow routine reads, writes, and local commands inside the current workspace, then ask before network access or crossing that boundary. Names and combinations differ across tools. Check the sandbox scope, when prompts appear, and who reviews them before choosing.

name: Sandbox
quote: Both sandboxing and command confirmation are meant to protect my computer. What does each one limit?
summaryLead: An isolated execution environment restricting the files, network, and system resources accessible by untrusted code or automated tasks.
summaryRest: For example, an AI tool may let commands write only inside the current workspace and restrict network access, reducing the chance that a bad script affects unrelated files. A sandbox may use OS controls, containers, or virtual machines, and its strength depends on the actual boundary. Mounted sensitive folders, injected real keys, and allowed networks remain accessible to code inside it.

name: TTFT / TPS
quote: Why do some AI tools take forever to show the first word while others answer right away?
summaryLead: Measures of time to first output and of token generation speed after output begins
summaryRest: TTFT measures time from sending a request to receiving the first token. TPS measures tokens produced each second afterward. A quick first token does not guarantee a short total response time.

summaryRest: System rules, chat history, files, tool results, and model output all use tokens across a multi-turn task. Cost also depends on the model and separate input, output, and cached-token prices; external tools may have their own fees.

summaryRest: After a limit is reached, a request may wait, slow down, or return 429. The exact limits vary by service, model, and account, so distinguish request, token, and concurrency limits.

Quick decision

Git merge vs rebase: which should you use?

Use Merge as the safer default for shared commits. Consider Rebase on an unshared personal branch when you want a linear history before review.

Decision pointGit MergeGit Rebase
Commit historyPreserves true branch history and explicit merge commits (or fast-forwards the branch pointer).Replays commits onto a new base, generating new commit hashes to produce a linear history.
CollaborationKeeps existing commit IDs, making shared history easier to integrate.Creates new commit IDs; rewriting shared history requires explicit team coordination.
When to useMerging a feature into main or integrating a shared team branch.Cleaning up an unshared personal branch or replaying it onto the latest main before review.
A feature branch with active collaborators

When teammates have already based work on your branch, Merge is the safer default because it does not rewrite commits they pulled. If the branch has not been shared, Rebase can place it on the latest main before review. Rewriting shared history should follow an explicit team agreement.

Quick decision

Pull request vs merge request: is there a difference?

They name the same general review-before-merge workflow. GitHub, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps use Pull Request (PR); GitLab uses Merge Request (MR). Product features still differ.

Decision pointPull Request (PR)Merge Request (MR)
Core conceptA proposal to review branch changes and discuss code diffs before merging into a target branch.GitLab's term for proposing, reviewing, and merging changes into a target branch.
Primary platformStandard terminology on GitHub, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps.Standard terminology on GitLab and GitLab CE/EE.
Product detailsReview rules, checks, and merge options depend on the hosting product and repository settings.Review rules, pipelines, and merge options depend on GitLab's edition and project settings.
Switching between GitHub and GitLab

On GitHub, a team opens a Pull Request; on GitLab, it opens a Merge Request. Both usually involve reviewing diffs, discussing changes, running checks, and approving a merge, but the available controls and rules depend on the platform and repository settings.

Design Principles

  • Use a small type and spacing system to create hierarchy

When to use it

name: Apple HIG
quote: I want that polished Apple website feel: big images, big type, and lots of white space.
summaryLead: Use precise hierarchy, generous space, and polished product imagery

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Give each section one clear message
  • Use large type with disciplined line length and spacing
  • Let product imagery explain real form and behavior
  • Keep controls familiar and visually precise
  • Use motion to connect states, not to delay the story

When to use it

  • Hardware or premium product launch
    The new one is here.
  • A focused feature story
    Sample priceBuy >
  • A brand with strong original imagery
    Let the visuals speak first
  • A page that can support careful art direction
    Forest Focus★ 4.9 · 1st place in efficiency category

When NOT to use it

  • Copy Apple's assets or interface details
    In a data-dense back-office tool, excessive whitespace wastes useful space.
  • Use huge headings when the content is weak
    Frosted glass everywhere
  • Hide basic information behind scroll effects
    Low-resolution images + mismatched corner radii + default typographyMismatched image and component details weaken the overall quality.
  • Apply glossy surfaces to an unrelated product
    Expense-report approval (80px between each field)Form tools should prioritize information density and completion efficiency.

A crisp edge and soft shadow create visual elevation; tune them to the component and surrounding surface.
Use gradients sparingly to add emphasis or suggest material depth, while preserving contrast.
Large, tightly set display type can create impact; test tracking and line breaks separately in Chinese and English.
Use generous whitespace to focus attention while keeping the next step and essential context visible.

name: Bento Grid
quote: Use one of those trendy feature sections made of differently sized tiles.
summaryLead: Arrange different kinds of content in a clear modular grid
summaryRest: A bento grid places feature cards of different sizes into one structured composition. Larger cells signal priority while smaller cells add supporting facts, media, or actions. The grid needs a reading order and responsive plan; varied card sizes alone do not create useful hierarchy.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Assign card size from content priority
  • Keep a clear reading path across the grid
  • Give each cell one focused job
  • Use shared spacing, corners, and surfaces to hold the set together
  • Recompose the grid deliberately for narrow screens

When to use it

  • Product feature overview
  • Portfolio or case-study index
    M4 chip10-core CPU · 18h battery life · 38 teraflops
  • Dashboard with several content types
    Feature page
  • Homepage section with visual variety

When NOT to use it

  • Give every card equal emphasis inside a supposedly varied grid
  • Place unrelated fragments together only to fill gaps
  • Force the desktop mosaic into one cramped mobile row
  • Use decorative cards that repeat the same message
    First step → Second step → Third step

Use different spans to express priorities; the reading order must still be maintained after rearrangement for small screens

Consistent spacing helps groups be identified; larger group spacing can be used when grouping is required
Title, description, data and actions are organized by priority, the number of elements is determined by the content

Design Principles

  • Keep text contrast stable across changing backgrounds

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Make the structure and interaction obvious
  • Use strong type and borders with a clear hierarchy
  • Choose a limited high-contrast palette
  • Let hard shadows describe layers consistently
  • Keep intentional irregularity separate from accidental disorder

When to use it

  • Creative studio or portfolio
    Stop overthinking. Ship it.An indie developer’s defiance and directness
  • Youth, culture, and event campaigns
    E-book ¥29Gumroad-style digital goods
  • A product with a direct, playful voice
    Hackathon 202648 hours
  • Small sites that benefit from strong identity
    “Anti-polish” is a stance too

When NOT to use it

  • Use constant visual shouting in a dense work tool
    Banking app (thick black outlines + fluorescent pink)Finance and healthcare need trust; a brutalist treatment can feel unreliable.
  • Sacrifice reading and focus states for attitude
    Enterprise tools need credibility, scanability, and clear states first.
  • Mix many unrelated colors, borders, and shadows
    Government service portal (high-contrast palette)Formal service contexts should prioritize dignity, stability, and ease of use.
  • Imitate roughness without a consistent layout
    × N pages

Feedback must be provided on hover, focus and pressed states, not just the mouse.

name: Swiss Style
quote: Use a strict grid, big type, and precise alignment so it feels clean like a poster.
summaryLead: Build clarity through grid, typography, and objective visual order
summaryRest: Swiss Style uses a strong grid, sans-serif type, asymmetric composition, and disciplined spacing to make information easy to scan. Its clean appearance comes from exact relationships, not from centering everything or removing all personality.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Use a visible grid to align text and images
  • Create hierarchy through type size, weight, and placement
  • Prefer clear information over decorative symbolism
  • Balance asymmetric groups across the composition
  • Keep spacing and column relationships consistent

When to use it

  • Poster-like campaign page
    We design systems.01 Brand 02 Book 03 Exhibition
  • Editorial index
    A Century of Bauhaus■ 2026.05 Shenzhen
  • Architecture or design portfolio
    2026Annual report
  • Information-rich page that needs strict order
    When images are unavailable, type can become the primary visual.

When NOT to use it

  • Place every element in the center
    Promotional campaign (black, white, and red)A promotional page needs a rhythm that fits the product and the desired action.
  • Use a grid without meaningful hierarchy
    Baby-products site (large Helvetica headlines)Categories that need warmth also need visual cues that support it.
  • Make type so rigid that long content becomes difficult to read
    Social app (grid + black and white)Social products also need expression that fits the community’s tone and interaction tasks.
  • Add decoration that fights the information structure
    A grid cannot replace content editing when priorities are unclear.

sections.title: Anatomy
sections.html:
Anatomy
strict grid AaSans-serif display type Accent color examples Large/Small Generous whitespace
Use a grid to organize alignment and spacing into a clear page structure.
Build hierarchy with deliberate type size and weight; align content according to language and layout relationships.
Use accent color for key information or actions, with its scope set by the brand and content hierarchy.
Create distinct reading levels with clear size and weight contrast while keeping supporting text legible.
Whitespace is an active part of the composition: it gives content room to breathe.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Let the story determine the visual rhythm
  • Pair expressive headlines with readable body text
  • Use images, captions, and pull quotes as real editorial material
  • Control line length and whitespace for long reading
  • Recompose the hierarchy for each screen size

When to use it

  • Magazine and culture site
    Thirty Years of a Tea CakeBrand Story · Issue 12
  • Brand story
    "Slowness is a kind of ability."
  • Long-form case study
    Spend a Week in the Mountains
  • Travel, fashion, or architecture feature
    Annual special issue2026

When NOT to use it

  • Use dramatic layouts around thin content
    Magazine-style layouts make a data back office harder to scan.
  • Make body text secondary to decoration
    Customer-service workspace (drop-cap version)High-frequency work interfaces should prioritize scanability and processing efficiency.
  • Copy a print spread without responsive behavior
    The Buy button is hidden at the end of the third column.Conversion pages: the CTA must not get lost in the layout.
  • Mix typefaces with no assigned editorial roles
    Keeping three columns on a phone makes lines too narrow.

Serif Aa serif title None Aa Sans serif text Column First Drop Cap VOL.12 · P.042Masthead page number

The text is sans-serif to keep it easy to read, and two types of fonts create hierarchy.
Narrow columns and short lines are the key to reading long articles. Remember to collapse to one column on small screens.
Use at the start of a suitable long article to introduce a paragraph. It does not suit every paragraph or language.
Create magazine-style editorial context with issue numbers, page numbers and column titles

name: Skeuomorphism
quote: Give it that early iPhone look, where buttons look like real buttons and notes look like actual notebooks.
summaryLead: Use familiar real-world form and material to explain a digital control
summaryRest: Skeuomorphism makes digital objects resemble physical ones through shape, texture, light, and behavior. It can make an unfamiliar interaction easier to understand or give a focused experience character. Literal leather, wood, and metal on every surface quickly add noise and age poorly.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Use the physical reference to clarify an interaction
  • Keep light, material, and depth internally consistent
  • Preserve readable labels and digital accessibility
  • Apply detail to a small number of important objects
  • Let digital behavior stay efficient even when the appearance is familiar

When to use it

  • Music and instrument interfaces
    Teaching older adults to use a tabletClick here to send a voice message
  • Games and playful tools
    DiaryA retro journaling app can use material cues to support its theme.
  • A focused control with a useful physical analogy
    WoodStringsRealistic control panels for cameras, recorders, and synthesizers
  • Brand experiences built around craft or material
    A strip of leather adds a small accent to an otherwise modern light interface.

When NOT to use it

  • Cover an entire work tool in decorative textures
    Body text sits on a textured background
  • Copy a physical limitation that makes the digital task slower
    One interface uses multiple material imagesAssess asset costs
  • Use realistic shading without clear interaction states
    Report CenterThe material treatment does not fit the task.
    Efficiency tools should prioritize clear data and controls.
  • Assume a physical reference is familiar to every audience
    Sign in

sections.title: History
sections.html:
History
2007.01
The iPhone brings skeuomorphism to touchscreens

Slide to unlock, page-turning calendars, and other physical references helped first-generation touchscreen users understand unfamiliar actions.

2010—2012
The peak of rich digital material

iOS 5 and 6 used yellow paper, wooden shelves, green felt, leather, and other detailed scenes across built-in apps.

2013.09
iOS 7 turns toward flat design

Apple removed most leather, linen, and realistic texture, and the wider industry quickly moved toward flatter interfaces.

2020s
Material returns as an accent

Neumorphism and spatial platforms brought back glass, depth, and physical material, usually as a supporting effect rather than the whole interface.

Anatomy
Memo Horizontal yellow paper + red margin line
Glass highlight button Linen pattern Real shadow
Brown gradient base, two dotted lines at the top and bottom serve as stitches, and the text is embossed with an inner shadow to create an indented feel.
Repeating gradient draws horizontal lines, a red margin line on the left, and handwriting-like fonts
Use light gradients and inner highlights to indicate smooth materials; use them only when needed to avoid affecting text
Two sets of intersecting fine repeating gradients, a classic base for large blank spaces
Large, soft, and ambient-colored projections make elements really appear to be floating on the desktop.

name: Flat Design
quote: No depth or shadows—just solid colors and simple shapes.
summaryLead: Use simple shapes, clear color, and minimal surface decoration
summaryRest: Flat design removes realistic texture and depth in favor of icons, type, color blocks, and direct layout. It scales well and keeps visual noise low, but interactive elements still need recognizable shapes, contrast, and states. Pure flatness that hides what is clickable is not useful simplicity.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Use simple shapes with clear roles
  • Create hierarchy through color, type, and spacing
  • Keep icons consistent and understandable
  • Make interactive elements visibly interactive
  • Use light depth cues when they improve usability
  • Build states that do not depend on texture

When to use it

  • Product interface
    Order exampleConversion exampleAlarm example
  • Responsive website
    Use simplified graphics first on small screens and slower connections.
  • Illustration and icon system
    Brand colorPurposeful use of brand color can support grouping and recognition.
  • A design system that needs broad reuse
    Start with solid color blocks and generous whitespace.→Verify structure

When NOT to use it

  • Remove every boundary around controls
    Welcome back
    View details · Submit order · Sign out    Text and interactive controls are hard to tell apart.
  • Use color alone to show interaction
    NavigationBodyButton
  • Make all surfaces visually equal
    The dialog and cards overlap, making it hard to tell which is in front.
  • Add flat icons that users cannot recognize
    A large blank area + one line of small textThe whitespace does not create a clear reading hierarchy.

sections.title: History
sections.html:
History
2010
Windows Phone introduces Metro

Solid tiles and oversized typography made flat design a system-level language several years before Apple's shift.

2013
iOS 7 moves fully into flat design

Apple removed most skeuomorphic detail, and flat interfaces became the new mainstream default.

2014
Material Design adds layers back

Google added elevation and purposeful motion to flat surfaces, restoring some of the hierarchy that pure flat design had lost.

2016–present
Flat 2.0 becomes the practical default

Light shadows and subtle gradients returned after teams learned that completely flat controls were often difficult to recognize.

sections.title: Anatomy
sections.html:
Anatomy
Solid color block Square or subtly rounded corners No shadows or gradients ◤ Lightweight type + open space
Use solid color blocks to separate areas and reinforce brand recognition; match saturation to the content and text contrast.
Choose square or subtly rounded corners consistently for the brand, component size, and touch target.
Avoid decorative shadows and gradients unless they clarify hierarchy or state.
Reduce icons to simple, recognizable geometric forms.
Use type scale, weight, and whitespace to establish hierarchy without overloading the page with detail.

name: Material Design
quote: Give it an Android-style look with layered cards and a ripple when people tap.
summaryLead: Use a systematic component language with clear layers and motion
summaryRest: Material Design is Google's design system for components, layout, color, type, elevation, and motion. Its value is the shared behavior and accessibility guidance, not making every product look like a Google app. Customize it through a consistent theme while keeping states and structure clear.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Build from reusable components and tokens
  • Use elevation only to explain layer relationships
  • Give every interactive state visible feedback
  • Let motion connect cause and result
  • Adapt the system to the brand without breaking consistency

When to use it

  • Android and cross-platform product
    Refer to Android’s component and interaction guidelines.
  • Large interface needing a mature component system
    Email
    you@example.com    Floating labels can clarify field names and input states.
  • Team that benefits from documented patterns
    A
    B
  • Rapid product work with accessibility requirements
    →

When NOT to use it

  • Copy default components without matching the product's content
  • Use elevation as decoration
    ＋✎ButtonLink
  • Mix several design systems in one flow
    ＋✎★
  • Customize each component independently until the system disappears
    Purple buttonHot-pink button

sections.title: History
sections.html:
History
2014.06
Material Design launches at Google I/O

Paper-like layers, ripple feedback, and the floating action button gave Android a shared system-wide design language.

2015—2017
Material spreads across Google's products

Gmail, Calendar, Maps, and other services adopted the system as the component ecosystem matured across platforms.

2018
Material Theming opens brand customization

Shape, color, and type became easier to customize in response to criticism that every Material app looked the same.

2021
Material You adds dynamic color

Android 12 introduced themes derived from a user's wallpaper, making the system more personal while keeping shared structure.

sections.title: Anatomy
sections.html:
Anatomy
Content layerFloating layer Brand primary color example ＋ Button Spacing scale
Use container, position, and moderate shading to illustrate who covers whom; intensity adjusts by component relationship
Assign stable color responsibilities to branding, status, and key actions and test readability on different backgrounds
Floating buttons can be used to initiate actions frequently; they do not have to appear on every page
Click feedback can spread outward from the touch point to indicate that the operation has been received
Establish reusable spacing and sizing relationships and allow exceptions for content, language, and accessibility needs

name: Neumorphism
quote: Make the buttons look like they're softly raised out of the background in the same color palette.
summaryLead: Use paired soft shadows to make controls appear pressed from one surface
summaryRest: Neumorphism, or Soft UI, uses highlights and shadows on nearly identical foreground and background colors. It can create a distinctive decorative object, but the low contrast often makes buttons, states, and boundaries difficult to perceive. Use it sparingly and test accessibility in real conditions.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Keep readable text and controls above contrast requirements
  • Use the effect on a small number of large surfaces
  • Add clear state changes beyond shadow direction
  • Maintain one consistent light source
  • Provide visible outlines or color where function depends on the boundary

When to use it

  • Concept art and visual experiments
    ⏮▶⏭
  • A decorative media control
    ◐
  • A small themed widget
    In everyday interfaces, limit neumorphism to noncritical areas.
  • Brand imagery where usability is not carried by the shadow alone
    12:30

When NOT to use it

  • Build a dense form or dashboard entirely from low-contrast surfaces
    Gray text and similar backgrounds reduce the readability of long text.
  • Use shadow direction as the only selected state
    Name?Button?
  • Place small controls in bright outdoor viewing conditions
    Buy now
  • Assume soft appearance means easy interaction
    In sunlight

sections.title: History
sections.html:
History
December 2019
A banking concept goes viral

Alexander Plyuto's concept showed controls appearing to press out of a same-colored surface and drew exceptional attention on design platforms.

2020
Soft UI reaches its peak

The style gained the name Neumorphism, and tutorials, UI kits, and generators appeared across the design community.

2020–2021
Accessibility criticism follows

Very low contrast made controls and backgrounds difficult to distinguish, especially in bright conditions, so real product adoption stayed limited.

Today
The style returns to a decorative role

Neumorphism now appears mainly in concept work, media controls, and isolated accents rather than complete production interfaces.

sections.title: Anatomy
sections.html:
Anatomy
Same color base #e3e9f2 ↖ white soft light ↘ gray-blue shadow Soft large rounded corners Depressed press
Use similar backgrounds to unify vision, but provide additional readable text and control boundaries.
Soft highlights can hint at the direction of the light source and should not be the only status indicator
Shadows can add volume; be strong enough not to interfere with text and focus
Fillet size follows component and brand; don’t make outlines difficult to recognize
The indentation effect can represent slots or levels, and active states should still use clear labels and feedback

name: SaaS Marketing Site
quote: Make it look like a software company website: a big hero headline, product screenshots, customer logos, and pricing.
summaryLead: Place the value, product proof, and next action on one clear reading path
summaryRest: A SaaS marketing site is a common website pattern, not a formal visual movement. It organizes a conversion path around the problem the product solves: a focused hero states the promise, real product views and customer evidence build trust, and a consistent call to action moves the visitor toward a trial or conversation. The visual style can vary, but decoration cannot replace product proof or a clear next step.

Design Principles
  • Make one promise above the fold: say who the product serves, what it changes, and why the visitor should keep reading
  • Show the real product early: a credible interface, workflow, or outcome explains more than an abstract glow

  • Keep one primary action: choose a trial, demo, or sales conversation as the main direction

When to use it

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Protect readability in the dark environment: body text, boundaries, and status cannot collapse into one gray layer
  • Give each signal color a job: running, success, risk, and the primary action should remain consistent
  • Show real content or product state: media, canvases, steps, logs, and results feel more credible than meaningless decoration
  • Use light effects to focus: local glow can emphasize a key area without covering every boundary

When to use it

  • Media, music, and creative tools where a dark environment lets the work itself remain central
    AGENT STATUS Service-status fieldLink-monitoring source
  • Developer tools, AI, and data products that can naturally show code, status, and console states
    > deploy intelligenceExecution-status field
  • Interfaces that support sustained focus, using layered grays to reduce irrelevant visual stimulation
    > deploy intelligenceExecution-status field
  • Brands expressing precision or immersion, where a dark base gives limited color and content more force
    AGENT STATUS Service-status fieldLink-monitoring source

When NOT to use it

  • Turn every element into neon; hierarchy disappears and sustained reading becomes tiring
    NEON EVERYTHINGGlow, grids and particles bury the product
  • Use random code as product proof; technical visitors will recognize the emptiness quickly
    NEON EVERYTHINGGlow, grids and particles bury the product
  • Set body text in thin, low-contrast gray; dark design still needs comfortable reading
    NEON EVERYTHINGGlow, grids and particles bury the product
  • Apply cyberpunk noise to a serious tool; glitch and clutter can undermine reliability
    NEON EVERYTHINGGlow, grids and particles bury the product

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Choose a clear period reference instead of mixing every retro trend
  • Use gloss, chrome, and transparency on focused elements
  • Balance playful display type with readable body text
  • Build a bright but controlled color palette
  • Let decoration frame content rather than cover it

When to use it

  • Music and youth-culture page
    ♪ Fan Hub · New Single Support Color: Ice BlueWorks for both player skins and fan-support pages.
  • Retro-future product launch
    ✦ Welcome to my homepage ✦ Message board · Photo album · Background musicA personal homepage can use it to express interests and identity.
  • Playful event or creator identity
    Limited collab · Retro Y2K pop-up, open for 7 days onlyShort-term campaign pages can use a more distinctive visual theme.

When NOT to use it

  • Cover text with sparkles and translucent decoration
    The provident fund inquiry page uses pink bubbles and glitterGovernment and financial pages should prioritize clarity and trustworthiness.
  • Use low-contrast chrome for functional labels
    The entire text section is made into a metallic gradient, which is hard to see due to glare.
  • Mix Y2K with unrelated retro periods
    Full page high saturation gradient
  • Apply a playful nostalgia theme to a serious operational tool
    Minimalist business+Y2K Bubble

sections.title: History
sections.html:
History
1998
The translucent iMac G3 arrives

Its bright Bondi Blue shell made visible plastic and friendly technology central images of the approaching millennium.

1999
The eve of the millennium

Anxiety about the Y2K bug existed alongside an optimistic fascination with what life after 2000 might look like.

2000-2004
Y2K style reaches popular culture

Chrome, bubblegum color, rhinestones, translucent gadgets, and customized mobile phones spread through music, fashion, and software.

2007-2015
Smartphones and flat design push it aside

Glossy surfaces began to feel dated as the iPhone era and flatter interface systems became dominant.

2020s
A new generation revives the period

People too young to remember the original moment rediscovered it as retro-futurism, and fashion and beauty brands followed.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Build a limited set of recurring shapes and patterns
  • Use strong color contrast with assigned roles
  • Separate decoration from text and controls
  • Balance asymmetry with a stable grid
  • Keep enough whitespace for the composition to breathe

When to use it

  • Campaign and promotion page
    The main visual of the brand event: contrasting banners + polka dots + zigzag linesCampaign pages can use Memphis design’s sense of rhythm.
  • Children's or education product after user testing
    English app for kids: use a geometry character in each lessonA lively sense of order supports course content and guidance
  • Creative studio and recruitment page
    Design studio recruitment page: contrasting color blocks + scattered trianglesIt can express a creative direction while keeping open roles and application instructions clear.
  • Illustration or empty-state area
    Empty state: polka dot circle, wavy line and "no content yet"Small areas of decoration can provide emotional support for status statements

When NOT to use it

  • Cover dense work interfaces in constant pattern
    A back-office system uses contrasting colors and scattered decoration across many pages.In a high-frequency tool, this reduces scanability and increases visual fatigue.
  • Place dots and shapes over reading or click targets
    Decoration that covers body copy reduces readability.
  • Mix a soft palette with heavy outlines without a reason
    A low-saturation palette can work too, as long as it fits the geometric language and content tone.
  • Let decoration overpower reports, contracts, or key facts
    An annual-report data page or contract-signing flow uses contrasting colors and scattered decoration.High-risk or formal flows should prioritize clear information and actions.

sections.title: History
sections.html:
History
1981
The Memphis Group forms in Milan

Ettore Sottsass and a group of young designers took their name from a Bob Dylan song playing during an early meeting.

1981–1987
The group challenges accepted good taste

Plastic laminate, contrasting color, and geometric pattern confronted the restrained rules of modernist design.

1987
The group ends, but the style spreads

After the group dissolved, its visual language continued through 1980s television, retail, music, and youth culture.

2010s
The internet rediscovers Memphis

As flat-design sameness grew tiring, Memphis shapes returned in campaign pages and illustration systems.

Today
The style remains common in campaigns

Dots, squiggles, and geometric shapes still appear in promotions, children's products, and creative brand sites.

sections.title: Anatomy
sections.html:
Anatomy
+ + + ++
Repeat a small set of geometric shapes to create a coherent decorative vocabulary.
Use primary and secondary contrasting colors for energy, while preserving readable text and status cues.
Dark outlines help small shapes separate from the background; tune their color and weight to the visual system.
Place small motifs along edges and in margins, leaving room for content and actions.
Use whitespace to separate content from decoration so high-contrast elements do not disrupt reading.

quote: Make it feel like a hacker terminal: black background, green text, monospace type, and command-line vibes.
summaryLead: Borrow command-line language to feel direct, technical, and tool-like
summaryRest: A terminal aesthetic uses monospaced type, prompts, command output, and a restrained palette. It suits developer tools and API documentation when the commands are real, searchable, and copyable. The whole page does not need to become green text on black.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Use monospace for commands, data, and short labels
  • Keep long explanations in a comfortable reading style
  • Use prompts and status symbols to clarify structure
  • Treat ASCII dividers as organization rather than decoration
  • Keep cursor animation subtle and respect reduced-motion settings

When to use it

  • Command-line tool website
    $ npx create-ai-appA CLI tool’s site can borrow cues from the command line.
  • Developer documentation
    docs/ ├─ quickstart.md └─ api.mdThe docs site uses monospaced type, making every navigation item look like command output.
  • API or cloud-service page
    POST /v1/chatSuccessful response · Sample delay
  • Engineering recruitment page
    $ whoami → backend engineer (remote)It can express engineering culture, but job details and application instructions must stay direct.

When NOT to use it

  • Assume non-technical visitors understand every terminal symbol
    The family photo album also uses green text on black.In nontechnical contexts, this style may offer few useful task cues.
  • Use low-contrast small text on a dark surface
    Dark green on black, made even smaller, becomes hard to read.
  • Turn commands into images that cannot be copied
    A terminal screenshot fills the first screen, leaving text unselectable and unsearchable.Keep commands as real text that people can copy and search.
  • Mix many unrelated glass and realistic effects into the same system
    $ runFrosted-glass bubbles

Prompts indicate command context; key operations, status, and errors still require text or stable icons

name: Wabi-sabi
quote: Make it a little more understated and weathered, with lots of open space and a quiet sense of age.
summaryLead: Use natural material, space, and asymmetry to create a quiet pace
summaryRest: Wabi-sabi-inspired web design draws from natural color, material texture, negative space, and hand-made variation to acknowledge time and imperfection. It is not one brand's style or a fixed beige-and-serif template. Real content, photography, and material should guide the choices.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Build a low-stimulation palette from real materials and imagery
  • Use space to slow the reading pace without losing structure
  • Choose type for the language and content
  • Create balanced asymmetry rather than random placement
  • Keep paper, clay, and grain textures behind the reading layer

When to use it

  • Home and craft brand
    Natural linen bedding · 4-piece setA home-goods brand site can use restrained materials and typography.
  • Tea, fragrance, and hand-made goods
    Handmade stoneware cups · Fired one kiln at a timeE-commerce for tea, incense, and tableware
  • Hospitality and travel site
    Mountain hot-spring inn · Check the booking page for live availabilityA guesthouse booking page can use a quiet visual rhythm to present the space.
  • Essay or personal blog focused on long reading
    "Autumn Memo" · Prose CollectionPersonal blogs and long-form reading

When NOT to use it

  • Reduce scan efficiency in a data-heavy tool
    Data dashboard: multiple charts + live KPI updatesIn task-dense contexts, prioritize scanability.
  • Add saturated accents with no clear role
    +
  • Use large empty areas without careful type and material detail
    One line of text on a plain white background, with no relationship to the contentWhitespace should support reading or showcase material, not stand in for information.
  • Interrupt the quiet rhythm with constant promotion labels
    50% off for a limited timeBestsellerNew arrival
    Too many promotional tags interrupt the reading rhythm.

sections.title: Anatomy
sections.html:
Anatomy
Off-white paper base+ + serif+ + + wa
An off-white, subtly textured surface can add warmth, provided it never interferes with legibility.
Draw colors from the product, photography, and brand while maintaining contrast for text and status.
Serif typography and measured letter spacing can set a calm reading rhythm; Chinese text must remain clear and legible.
Use space to pace the composition and clarify relationships; let content and screen size determine the proportions.
Create asymmetrical balance through content, alignment, and open space rather than forcing perfect symmetry.
Use saturated accents sparingly for a signature detail or key emphasis, not as a page-wide requirement.

name: Bauhaus
quote: I want a geometric page—circles, squares, triangles—and every shape has to do a job, not just some color blocks.
summaryLead: Organize the page with basic geometry, honest materials, and function
summaryRest: Exhibition and brand pages often let circles, squares, and triangles carry division, direction, and emphasis directly, with color only marking those functional relationships. If a page just spreads red, yellow, and blue blocks while the content organization stays unchanged, it borrowed the palette, not the Bauhaus.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Compose with basic shapes: circles, squares, triangles
  • Give every shape a job: dividing, pointing, emphasizing
  • Reserve primary colors for functional relationships
  • Set headlines in plain, bold sans-serif type
  • Keep asymmetric layouts visually balanced

Bauhaus≠Swiss Style

Swiss Style communicates through a strict text grid and objective typography; in Bauhaus, geometry itself is the structure that organizes the page.

Bauhaus≠Neo-Brutalism

Neo-Brutalism uses heavy borders, hard shadows, and raw default controls for confrontation; Bauhaus composition serves function and balance instead.

When to use it

  • Museum, exhibition, and cultural institution sites
    Design Archive ShowJun 12 – Sep 30
  • Brand launches that build recognition through geometry
    New brand launch
  • Design courses and workshops that emphasize structure
    Week 1: Circles and Balance
    Week 2: Squares and Sections
  • Cultural events that need a poster-like hero
    A Night of GeometryAn event page with a poster-like hero

When NOT to use it

  • Spreading red-yellow-blue blocks while the content structure stays the same
  • Adding shapes that relate to nothing on the page
  • Layering shapes until headlines and body text become hard to read
    An unreadable headline
  • Setting long paragraphs in heavy geometric display type
    Body copy in heavy display type tires after two lines

sections.title: History
sections.html:
History
1919
The Bauhaus school opens in Weimar

Walter Gropius founded the Bauhaus in Weimar, aiming to reunite art, craft, and technology in design.

1923
The visual language matures

Basic geometry, primary colors, and functionalism took shape across the school's courses and exhibitions.

1933
The school closes, its influence spreads

The school closed under political pressure; its teachers and students carried its methods into modern design education worldwide.

sections.title: Anatomy
sections.html:
Anatomy
Shape = function Primary accents Sans-serif headlines Asymmetric balance
Circles, squares, and triangles are the smallest units of the composition
Every shape divides, points, or emphasizes; nothing is idle decoration
Red, yellow, and blue only mark functional relationships, in restrained areas
Bold headlines with direct hierarchy and no ornamental letterforms
Elements need not be centered or mirrored, yet the visual weight stays stable

name: Art Deco
quote: I want a vintage-luxury page—symmetrical composition with geometric motifs, like an old theater poster, not just gold text.
summaryLead: Express modern luxury through symmetry, stepped contours, and radiating motifs
summaryRest: Hotel, jewelry, and event pages often organize the page around a mirrored central axis, ziggurat-like stepped shapes, and sunburst rays, with metallic color as only the final sheen. A page that merely turns its headings and buttons gold while the skeleton stays ordinary is not Art Deco.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Build a mirrored skeleton around a central axis
  • Shape contours that step inward layer by layer
  • Use sunburst, fan, and zigzag geometric motifs
  • Create refinement with fine lines and repetition
  • Keep metallic sheen as a small-area accent

Art Deco≠Black-and-gold palette

Black and gold is just a palette that any style can use; Art Deco is judged by its skeleton of symmetry, stepped contours, and radiating motifs.

Art Deco≠Art Nouveau

Art Nouveau uses plant-like long curves and organic forms; Art Deco uses symmetrical geometry and straight or zigzag lines. They are close in era but opposite in shape language.

When to use it

  • Boutique hotel, jewelry, and watch websites
    HOTEL LUMIÈRERiver-view suites · Book now
  • Vintage theater, gala, and exhibition event pages
    Jazz NightFridays 8 PM
  • Craft-led luxury products such as perfume and whisky
    Geometry of Light18K gold
  • Award and ceremony feature pages
    Annual Awards CeremonyCeremony and award features

When NOT to use it

  • Turning headings and buttons gold while the skeleton stays unchanged
    A gold headlineA gold button
  • Using plant vines and long curves, which belong to Art Nouveau
  • Spreading motifs across body text until it becomes unreadable
    Body text over motifs is unreadable
  • Dropping misaligned elements into a symmetrical composition

sections.title: History
sections.html:
History
1925
The Paris exposition names the style

The Exposition internationale des arts décoratifs et industriels modernes in Paris gave the style its name and momentum.

1920s–30s
Into architecture and popular graphics

Stepped contours and geometric motifs appeared on skyscrapers, theaters, posters, and luxury goods, defining modern luxury.

1930s
Global spread and local variants

Art Deco spread worldwide, leaving distinct local variants in cities such as Shanghai, Miami, and Mumbai.

sections.title: Anatomy
sections.html:
Anatomy
Metallic accent
The page mirrors itself along a central axis; order comes from symmetry
Borders step inward layer by layer, like a skyscraper setback
Sunburst or fan shapes unfold from a single center
Gold or brass appears in small areas, attached to the skeleton

name: Paywall Design
quote: I want one of those upgrade screens top apps use to make paying feel obvious — same layout tricks, same wording.
summaryLead: Paywall design turns the 'to pay or not' moment into the most deliberately crafted screen in the app
summaryRest: Top subscription apps converge on the same structure: a one-line value promise, 3–5 concrete benefits, a monthly/annual price anchor, a free trial paired with 'cancel anytime' reassurance, and an unobtrusive exit. Appllama catalogs 1,200+ real paywalls and onboarding flows from leading iOS apps — the reference library for this design family.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Open with one value promise: sell the upgraded self before the features
  • Benefits must be countable and concrete: 3–5 lines, each with an icon
  • Anchor monthly against yearly: highlight the annual plan and its savings
  • Pair the trial with reassurance: 'no charge · cancel anytime' under the button
  • Give an exit, but not attention: a faint ✕ top-right, small print for downgrade

Paywall≠Popup ad

A paywall persuades at the moment of peak demand with a value story; a popup interrupts indiscriminately for exposure. Test: would you pay for what this page offers?

Paywall≠Pricing page

A pricing page helps people compare plans; a paywall drives one decision — one primary button, two or three tiers, no branching.

sections.title: AI Prompt
sections.html:
AI Prompt

Design an app upgrade screen: one value-promise headline, 3 benefits with icons; monthly and yearly tiers side by side, yearly highlighted with 'save 40%'; primary gradient button 'Start 7-day free trial' with 'no charge · cancel anytime' beneath it; a faint ✕ close in the top-right; leave marked placeholders where real copy is missing.

name: Dark Library
quote: I want that Appllama feeling: dark ground, dense cards, a touch of gold — a site that visibly holds a library.
summaryLead: Dark Library is the style of near-black grounds, a single gold accent and dense card grids — turning a content site into an archive with ceremony
summaryRest: It wins on three moves: dark removes ambient noise so cover art becomes the only light source; one accent color (usually gold) used sparingly is what reads as premium; and high card density sells 'volume' itself as credibility. The cost: long-form reading and colorful demos need adaptation work.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Ground near-black but not pure (#141519 range); cards sit one step brighter — layer by lightness, not shadows
  • One accent site-wide: gold only on brand marks, active filters and the primary CTA
  • Dense cards: logo, name, one line — tighten leading, drop decoration
  • Cover art is the protagonist: lift imagery to near-white-ground brightness so it glows
  • Cool grays for text: #ECEEF2 primary, #8B8E99 secondary — no big blocks of pure white
  • Light and dark are one design: same layout, swapped ramps — selection is a gold outline on dark, a cream fill on light; the three-step grey inverts with the theme

Dark Library≠Dark UI

Dark UI is just the inverted palette applied anywhere; Dark Library adds hard constraints — one gold accent and a collectible, dense card grid. It sells the feeling of a stocked archive.

Dark Library≠Neo-Brutalism

Both dare with strong color, but brutalism is light ground, thick black borders, hard shadows; Dark Library is quiet layers of lightness on dark ground.

sections.title: AI Prompt
sections.html:
AI Prompt

Restyle this content site as a Dark Library: ground #141519, cards #20222A layered by brightness without shadows; the only accent is gold #E8C767, limited to brand mark, active filter chips and primary buttons; card grid 3-4 per row with logo + name + one line; wrap existing interactive demos in a light 'viewing card' to avoid color casts. Keep all functionality and copy unchanged.Also provide the matching light-theme values (cards #FFFFFF, borders #E4E4E7, text #1A1B20); both modes share one layout — the theme switch only changes tokens.

name: Scrapbook Journal
quote: I want it to feel like a personal collection journal: warm paper ground, serif display titles, cards tilted slightly as if pasted in by hand.
summaryLead: Scrapbook Journal brings the physicality of a personal collection into the web: paper-toned ground, serif display type, slightly rotated cards and tape-like accents
summaryRest: It fits a catalog site's identity naturally — the whole site is a field notebook, so the surfaces should feel collected rather than manufactured: small rotations, uneven cards, one hand-made accent. The restraint rule: exactly one decorative vocabulary per page, or it slides from journal into sticker war.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Paper ground (#F5EFE2 range) instead of pure white, so white cards read as pasted-on sheets
  • Serif or rounded display type for titles; body stays sans for readability
  • Cards rotated ±1-2° with a 2px hard shadow — pasted down, not floating
  • One decorative vocabulary only: tape, paperclip or stamp — never together
  • Emphasis as sticky note: a partial yellow block behind key content, not a new brand color
  • Night-paper mode swaps material, not layout: paper turns black cardstock, tapes desaturate, the highlight shifts from cream to dark gold — tape and notes stay legible

Scrapbook Journal≠Editorial

Editorial builds order from strict grids and gutters; Journal deliberately breaks a little order (rotation, stagger) for human warmth. Opposite directions, both valid.

Scrapbook Journal≠Organic Design

Organic is earthy colors and soft shapes — 'nature'; Journal is about traces of hand-arrangement — paper, tape, stamps.

name: Catalog Navbar
quote: The site keeps growing, but visitors land without knowing what to browse or where to look.
summaryLead: A catalog navbar spreads the whole content map into one persistent top bar: sections, a feature pill, site-wide search, upgrade and identity — each in its lane.
summaryRest: Appllama is the archetype: logo wordmark + Apps/Explore/Pricing laid flat + a black pill feature slot + a search field with a / shortcut hint + Go Pro and an avatar to close. It sells the browsing ritual of a directory — you know where you are and where to go within three seconds. BuildHub maps directly: Terms / Skills / Products / Prompts + search + a PRO slot.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • One bar, four jobs: sections, a feature pill, site-wide search, identity & upgrade — never a fifth
  • Lay sections flat, no hover menus: cap top-level zones at 5–7; if it overflows, restructure content before nesting
  • Search is a first-class citizen: pinned right after the sections, always visible, with a / or ⌘K hint, opening a command palette
  • PRO sits on the outer edge: a Go Pro text link beside the avatar — never competing with sections, never a popup
  • Light and dark share one layout: the pill goes solid on light, outlined on dark; bar height and spacing never change

Catalog Navbar≠Mega Menu

A mega menu drops a two-tier panel on hover for sprawling catalogs; the catalog navbar stays flat — built for directory-style content sites with few top-level zones.

Catalog Navbar≠Sidebar docs nav

Sidebars serve deep, single-track reading; the top tool belt serves horizontal browsing — hopping between zones, not drilling one tree.

sections.title: AI Prompt
sections.html:
AI Prompt

Restyle the BuildHub header as a catalog navbar: logo tile + wordmark on the left; top-level sections laid flat in the middle (Terms / Skills / Products / Prompts, no dropdowns); one pill right after the sections as the featured slot (Assets); a persistent rounded search field with a / shortcut badge that opens a command palette; on the far right a Go Pro text link plus a round avatar (theme & language switch live inside it). 56px bar, 1px bottom border, light and dark share the layout — only tokens swap. Keep every existing route and feature; don't touch copy.

name: Native iOS
quote: I want that built-in Apple app feel: system font, system colours, clean lists, no custom controls.
summaryLead: Native iOS follows Apple's Human Interface Guidelines to the letter: SF system type, collapsing Large Title navigation, inset grouped lists and a translucent tab bar, with almost no custom decoration
summaryRest: It gets three things right: controls look like part of the system, so there is zero learning cost; hierarchy comes from size and whitespace, never from colour; both appearances flip automatically through semantic colours. The cost is memorability — apps in this style blur into each other, and the brand has to live in one accent colour and the icon.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Stock controls only: NavigationStack / List (inset grouped) / TabView — no hand-drawn buttons, cards or switches
  • SF Pro throughout; build hierarchy with 34 / 22 / 17 / 15 / 13pt steps, not with colour
  • Large Title collapses into a centred inline title on scroll — no custom banner at the top
  • Inset grouped lists: 16pt side margins, 10–14pt corner radius, 0.5pt hairline separators
  • 49pt translucent tab bar; the selected state only changes tint, never adds a fill or outline
  • Semantic colours only (label / secondaryLabel / systemBackground / separator) — hard-coded #fff and #000 are banned, dark mode flips for free

Easy to confuse? Here is the line
Native iOS≠Apple HIG marketing style

Our Apple HIG entry describes apple.com marketing pages — oversized type, enormous whitespace, product photography as the hero. This one is the working screen inside an app; there is no hero at all.

Native iOS≠Minimalism

Minimalism is an aesthetic choice — you may drop every border. Native iOS is an engineering constraint: system components and semantic colours are mandatory. Fitting into the system outranks looking distinctive.

sections.title: AI Prompt
sections.html:
AI Prompt

Restyle this app as Native iOS: use stock components only (NavigationStack, List with inset grouped style, TabView) — no custom buttons, cards or switches; SF Pro with Large Title 34pt bold → section header 22pt → body 17pt → caption 13pt secondary, no webfonts; colours limited to system semantics (label / secondaryLabel / systemBackground / secondarySystemBackground / separator) so dark mode flips automatically; one single tint (#0A84FF) reserved for selection, primary actions and switches; navigation bar collapses with a translucent material on scroll. Keep every feature and string as is.

name: Soft Wellness
quote: I want the Calm feeling: soft as you open it, milky colours, round corners, puffy cards.
summaryLead: Soft Wellness is the shared look of meditation, sleep, habit and mental-health apps: a low-saturation gradient filling the screen, oversized rounded cards, rounded display type and a hand-drawn or 3D mascot
summaryRest: It gets three things right: colour sets the mood before content arrives; big radii and whitespace turn tool-feel into companionship; the mascot carries progress, so users feel encouraged rather than scored. The cost is density — serious contexts such as finance or productivity look unprofessional in it.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • One low-saturation gradient fills the screen (sky / sunset / night); content floats on it — no white card wall
  • Corner radius up to 20–28pt, pill buttons, wide soft shadows; never a 1pt hard border
  • Rounded display face for headings (Saans, Sofia, Quicksand), weight capped at 600, size 28–34pt
  • Accents grouped by emotion rather than brand: sleep purple, breath orange, activity green — one family per screen
  • The mascot owns empty, loading and completed states; celebration motion stays slow (400ms+, ease-out)
  • Dark mode is a night edition, not an inversion: layout untouched, gradient swapped to deep blue-violet, artwork dimmed

Easy to confuse? Here is the line
Soft Wellness≠Neumorphism

Neumorphism is a pure technique — same-colour extruded shadows that can dress any subject. Soft Wellness is a mood built from gradients, illustration and rounded type, and its subject is fixed to wellbeing.

Soft Wellness≠Kawaii

Cute can be loud: saturated, multicoloured, sticker-covered. Soft Wellness must stay quiet — desaturated, slow, exactly one visual focus per screen.

sections.title: AI Prompt
sections.html:
AI Prompt

Restyle this app as Soft Wellness: a low-saturation gradient fills every screen (day #F8DCC3→#DCB8E8, night #1B1E3C→#3A2F5C) with cards floating on it; 24pt card radius, pill buttons, wide soft shadows (0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.08)), no 1pt borders; rounded display headings at 28–34pt / weight 600, body 16; one emotional palette per area (sleep purple #6C5CE7, breath orange #FF8F5E, activity green #4CAF7D) instead of a single brand colour; a small mascot owns empty and completed states, motion never under 400ms with ease-out. Layout and copy unchanged, both appearances share the components.

name: Dark Pro Tool
quote: For an editing app: black interface, dense information, one blue accent, and no illustrations eating my screen.
summaryLead: Dark Pro Tool is the shared look of video, photo, music and 3D tools: a near-black ground, a single cold accent, dense persistent toolbars, and most of the screen handed to the work itself
summaryRest: It gets three things right: dark keeps the colours of the artwork honest; persistent, flattened toolbars stop interrupting professionals; the accent marks only what is selected, everything else stays grey. The cost is a steep learning curve, and once the artwork is colourful the interface carries no brand at all. It is the one style here that explicitly skips the light theme.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Ground near black (#1C1C1E–#232326); panels sit one step brighter — layer by lightness, not borders
  • A single cold accent (blue #0A84FF or cyan-violet) marks the active tool and active value; everything else is grey
  • Persistent, icon-first toolbars: no text buttons, no onboarding bubbles, at most two levels deep
  • Canvas and timeline take at least 70% of the screen; controls compress to 28–36pt while hit areas stay 44pt
  • Numerics right-aligned in a monospaced face; sliders show exact values and ticks — professionals need reproducibility
  • No light theme: creators work in the dark and a light ground misrepresents the work (the one light-mode exemption on this site)

Easy to confuse? Here is the line
Dark Pro Tool≠Dark Library

Dark Library is a content site's cabinet — gold accents and dense cards selling the size of a collection, and its job is browsing. Dark Pro Tool is a workbench: its job is doing, so decoration is removed and the accent turns cold.

Dark Pro Tool≠Turning dark mode on

Dark mode is an inverted copy of the same light UI — whitespace and density untouched. Dark Pro Tool's density, persistent toolbars and monospaced values were designed for a dark workbench; light versions of it look visibly worse.

sections.title: AI Prompt
sections.html:
AI Prompt

Restyle this app as Dark Pro Tool: ground #1C1C1E, panels #26272B layered by lightness without borders; one accent #0A84FF reserved for the selected tool and active value; text limited to #FFFFFF and #9A9AA0; a persistent top toolbar of icons (24×24 glyphs on 44pt hit areas), no text buttons and no coach marks; canvas and timeline occupy at least 70% of the screen, controls 28–36pt tall; all numerics monospaced and right-aligned, sliders showing exact values with ticks. Keep the features, and do not build a light theme.

name: Calm Console
quote: Make my workbench feel like Linear: grey-white ground, hairline borders, small dense type, one hint of violet — quiet, but expensive.
summaryLead: Calm Console is the shared visual language of mainstream productivity workbenches like Linear, Vercel and Raycast: neutral grey-white grounds, 1px hairline layering, small dense type and a single low-saturation accent
summaryRest: The premium comes from restraint, not elements: no shadows or gradients — layers are pulled apart by borders and gray ramps; every number is tabular so metrics read like instruments; status lives in micro badges, not color blocks. The cost is that it never startles — quiet at first glance, and thin if content density is low.

sections.title: Design Principles
sections.html:
Design Principles
  • Ground is neutral grey-white only: light page #FAFAFA / cards #FFFFFF, dark page #101112 / cards #18191A — no blue or warm cast; premium starts with zero color noise
  • Layer with 1px hairlines, not shadows: #E4E4E7 light, #292A2E dark — borders visible but never loud; no gradients, no decorative illustration
  • One accent site-wide (violet around #5E6AD2, lifted to #8B93E8 in dark), reserved for the primary action, selection and links — under 5% of the viewport
  • Small type, high density: 13px body, 12px meta, restrained headings; every number, date and count uses tabular-nums so metric columns align like instruments
  • Status lives in low-saturation micro badges: green in-progress / amber at-risk / grey todo — 10% alpha fill with a same-hue border, never shouting color blocks
  • Light and dark are one design: layout and components never move — the three-step gray ramp and borders flip wholesale, the accent lifts one step, selection keeps the same 1px-outline grammar

Calm Console≠Dark Pro Tool

Both sell 'professional', but Dark Pro Tool is creative-tool chrome — near-black canvas, dense always-on toolbar, the screen belongs to the work. Calm Console is a management panel — grey-white boards and modules where the screen belongs to data and status.

Calm Console≠Dark UI

Dark UI is just the inverted palette applied anywhere; Calm Console is about density and restraint — hairline borders, a single accent, tabular numerals. Its light mode looks just as premium, which proves the style never relied on darkness.

sections.title: AI Prompt
sections.html:
AI Prompt

Restyle this workbench in the Calm Console language: light mode page #FAFAFA, cards #FFFFFF, borders #E4E4E7, text #18191A/#6B6E76/#A1A1AA; dark mode page #101112, cards #18191A, borders #292A2E, text #E4E4E7/#8A8F98/#5C6066. One accent only — #5E6AD2 (dark: #8B93E8) — limited to primary buttons, selection and links. No shadows, no gradients. 13px body, 12px meta, and font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every number; status uses low-saturation micro badges (green/amber/grey, 10% alpha fill with same-hue border). Keep all existing features and copy untouched; both modes share one layout and component set — theming flips tokens only.
